components.name: Box
components.summary: Box is a plain block for an inset, a size container or a named region, with no layout of its own.
useWhen: Content needs an inset and nothing else, such as a region of a page.
The application's style sheet queries a region's width, through a named size container.
A region should show up by name in dev mode and the docs.

avoidWhen.text: Children one under another with gaps.
Children side by side with gaps.
Children in columns.
A background, a border or corners.

examples.name: InsetRegion
examples.title: Inset region
examples.description: Box is a plain block for an inset, a size container or a name, with no layout of its own. Like Row, Column and Grid, it sizes to its content and never paints.

examples.name: SizeContainer
examples.title: Size container
examples.description: `container="summary"` makes the box a size container that the application's style sheet can query, such as `@container summary (width >= 37.5rem)`. Give one in a flex row a width of its own: a container takes its width from its context, never from its content.

examples.name: OneInset
examples.title: Do: One inset on the region, and a Column inside for the gaps.

examples.name: BoxPerChild
examples.title: Don't: A padded box around each child: every gap is different.

components.name: Row
components.summary: Row lays out content side by side with even gaps, and wraps when it doesn't fit, such as a form's actions.
useWhen: A few actions belong together, such as a form's Cancel and Save, in a row that wraps.
A heading and its actions share a line, with the actions at the end.
Small items sit side by side, such as a label and a badge.

avoidWhen.text: Content top to bottom.
Content in columns of equal or set widths, such as cards.
Buttons joined into one connected control, such as a main action beside a menu of alternatives.
Controls for one subject that the arrow keys move between, such as an editor's formatting.

examples.name: FormActions
examples.title: Form actions
examples.description: Row lays out its children side by side, the same step of the spacing scale apart. Like Column, Grid and Box, it sizes to its content and never paints.

examples.name: WrappingActions
examples.title: Do: wrap, so an action that doesn't fit moves to the next line.

examples.name: SqueezedActions
examples.title: Don't: No wrap in a narrow pane: the labels break inside their buttons.

components.name: Column
components.summary: Column lays out content one under another with even gaps, such as a heading, text and a form.
useWhen: Content runs top to bottom with even space between, such as a heading, text and a form.
Sections and their contents need different spacing, by nesting columns with different gaps.
Actions in a narrow pane need the whole width for their labels, stacked with fullWidth buttons.

avoidWhen.text: Children side by side, such as a form's actions.
Content in columns, such as cards or a main column beside its details.
An inset or a size container around content, without a column of its own.
A background, an inset and corners around content.
A block with a heading, metadata and actions.

examples.name: ProjectDetails
examples.title: Project details
examples.description: Column lays out its children one under another, the same step of the spacing scale apart, so the children need no margins. Like Row, Grid and Box, it sizes to its content and never paints.

examples.name: CenteredContent
examples.title: Alignment
examples.description: `align` keeps each child at its own width, at the `start`, `center` or `end`; the default, `stretch`, makes each as wide as the column. Buttons, chips and badges keep their own width in any case.

examples.name: NestedSpacing
examples.title: Do: A larger gap between sections and a smaller one inside them.

examples.name: OneGapForAll
examples.title: Don't: One gap for everything: the sections run together.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: Grid lays out content in columns, a set number, a template or as many as fit, with even gaps.
useWhen: Items of one kind fill the width in as many columns as fit, such as cards or stats.
A main column sits beside a narrower one, such as a summary and its details.
Content lines up in a set number of equal columns.

avoidWhen.text: Content top to bottom, one item per line.
A few items side by side at their own widths, such as actions.
Rows of data that people sort, select or compare.
Two panes people resize, or a list beside its detail.

examples.name: ProjectCards
examples.title: Project cards
examples.description: Grid lays out its children in columns, the same step of the spacing scale apart. Like Row, Column and Box, it sizes to its content and never paints.

examples.name: FittingColumns
examples.title: Do: A minimum width, so the grid fits the columns to its own width.

examples.name: FixedColumns
examples.title: Don't: Three columns in a narrow pane: each card is squeezed.

components.name: Scaffold
components.summary: The invisible structure of an application's screen, with a top bar region, the navigation and the body, which shows the navigation form that fits its own width and keeps the bars in view as the page scrolls.
useWhen: An application's screen, with a top bar, its navigation and the page people are on.
A window without navigation, such as a start page, with its title bar above the body.

avoidWhen.text: A readable column for a page's content, with its gutters.
Two panes side by side inside the body, such as a list and its detail.
Rows, columns and grids inside a page.

examples.name: NavigationForms
examples.title: Navigation forms
examples.description: Scaffold is the invisible structure of an application's screen: a top bar, the navigation and the body. It never paints; the components in its regions do. It shows the navigation form that fits its own width, the Bar, the Rail or the Drawer, so give it all three with the same destinations.

examples.name: ChooseForms
examples.title: Navigation by window class
examples.description: | Window class | Width of the Scaffold | Form | | ------------ | --------------------- | -------- | | compact | below 37.5 rem | `bar` | | medium | 37.5 to 52.5 rem | `rail` | | expanded | 52.5 to 75 rem | `drawer` | | large | from 75 rem | `drawer` | `forms` changes the form of a window class, or shows `none`. Where a window class asks for a form the application didn't give, the nearest given one shows.

examples.name: TitleBarAcross
examples.title: A title bar across
examples.description: `topBarSpan="full"` runs the top bar across the whole width, above the rail or the drawer, as a window's title bar needs.

examples.name: ActionsInPageHeader
examples.title: Do: The page's title and actions in its PageHeader.

examples.name: ActionsInTopBar
examples.title: Don't: The page's title and action in the top bar: the page has no heading.

parts.description: The scaffold: the top bar, navigation and body regions; it never paints.
The slot of the navigation bar, at the bottom of a compact window.
The body, the main region, which scrolls.
The slot of the navigation drawer, at the start from expanded.
The navigation region, which holds a slot per form.
The slot of the navigation rail, at the start of a medium window.
One link that skips to the body or the navigation.
The skip links, shown on keyboard focus.
The top bar region, the banner.

components.name: Panes
components.summary: Two panes side by side, after Material's pane patterns, that behave as a main pane with a supporting sheet or as a list and its detail when there is less room.
useWhen: A main pane with a supporting pane beside it, such as a document and its details, which becomes a sheet where there is no room.
A list beside the chosen item's detail, which shows one at a time where there is no room.

avoidWhen.text: An application's screen with its top bar and navigation.
Columns of cards or fields that wrap, inside a page.
A panel that opens over the page from an edge on demand.

examples.name: SupportingPane
examples.title: Supporting pane
examples.description: `behavior="supporting"`: a main pane and a supporting one, such as a document and its details. In less room the supporting pane is a modal sheet while `open`.

examples.name: ResizableDetails
examples.title: Resizable
examples.description: Panes.Divider resizes the supporting pane or the list, by pointer and the arrow keys. `persist` keeps the width people choose in a cookie; read it on the server with `readPanesSize` and pass it as `persistedSize`, so nothing moves as the page hydrates.

examples.name: DetailsButton
examples.title: Do: A button in the main pane that opens the details where there is no room.

examples.name: NoWayToDetails
examples.title: Don't: No button: in less room, the details can't be reached.

examples.name: BackToInbox
examples.title: Do: A backLabel that names where the back button goes.

examples.name: GenericBack
examples.title: Don't: Back alone: people can't tell where it leads.

parts.description: The panes: two panes side by side, or how they behave in less room; it never paints.
The button back to the list, when one pane shows at a time.
The supporting sheet's close button, which shows only while the pane is a sheet.
The detail pane of list-detail panes.
The divider that resizes the panes.
The list pane of list-detail panes.
The main pane of supporting panes.
The scrim behind the supporting sheet.
The supporting pane, a sheet over the main pane in less room.
A handle that resizes a region.

components.name: Page
components.summary: The invisible column a page's content sits in, centered at a readable width with the page gutter by window class, and the page's header at its top.
useWhen: A page's content needs a readable width in a wide window, such as a form, a document or a dashboard.
A page has a heading with actions above its content, passed as its header.

avoidWhen.text: The frame of an application, with its top bar and navigation.
Content in a column or a row with even gaps inside a page.
A background, an inset and corners around a part of a page.
Two panes side by side, such as a list and its detail.

examples.name: WithHeader
examples.title: With header
examples.description: Page is the column a page's content sits in: a readable width, the page gutter and the page's header at its top. It never paints and adds no landmark; it goes in a Scaffold's body, which is the main.

examples.name: HeaderInPage
examples.title: Do: The heading in header, in the page's column and gutter.

examples.name: HeaderOutside
examples.title: Don't: A PageHeader outside the page: it doesn't line up with the content.

parts.description: The page: a readable width and the gutter; it never paints.
The page's content at its width.

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: A page's heading row, with its title, an optional trail and description, its actions and a toolbar row, that wraps to its own width and can stick to the top.
useWhen: A page opens with its title and the actions that apply to the whole page, such as New project.
A page needs its trail, a status or a count beside its title, or a row of search and filters under it.
The page's heading should stay in view as the page scrolls.

avoidWhen.text: The application's bar across every page, with its name, search and account menu.
The heading of a section inside a page, with its own actions.
A heading with metadata and actions around a block of content.
Controls for one subject that the arrow keys move between.

examples.name: WithBreadcrumbs
examples.title: With breadcrumbs
examples.description: A page header holds a page's title, with an optional trail, description, meta and the page's actions. Put it in a Page's `header`.

examples.name: WithToolbar
examples.title: With toolbar
examples.description: `toolbar` adds a row below the title for search, filters and view switches. `controlSize="sm"` gives the buttons in `actions` and `toolbar` the small height of a dense page.

examples.name: Sticky
examples.title: Sticky
examples.description: With `sticky`, the header stays at the top of the area that scrolls, under a Scaffold's top bar. What takes focus in the page keeps clear of it.

examples.name: PageActions
examples.title: Do: Actions for this page, with the primary one last.

examples.name: FrameActions
examples.title: Don't: The account and sign-out in a page's header: they belong to the frame.

examples.name: NameTheContent
examples.title: Do: A title that names what the page holds.

examples.name: InstructionAsTitle
examples.title: Don't: An instruction as the title, and a description that repeats it.

parts.description: The column with the title and the description.
The row with the title and the actions.
The content before the title, such as an avatar or a back button.
The line with the title and the meta.

components.name: Surface
components.summary: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own.
useWhen: A region needs a background, an inset and corners, such as a detail pane or a side panel.
A block should stand apart from what is around it, such as a summary on a pane.
A toolbar floats over dense content, such as a diagram, with small controls inside.

avoidWhen.text: Content with a heading, metadata and actions, or a block people press to open something.
Rows of items that people scan, each with a label, a description and actions.
Space between children without a background.
Content over the page that people dismiss, such as a form in a window.
A floating panel that opens from a button.

examples.name: DetailPane
examples.title: Detail pane
examples.description: A surface gives a region a background, an inset and rounded corners, and nothing else. Lay out what it holds with a Column or a Row through `render`, so the surface and its layout are one element.

examples.name: BlockOnPane
examples.title: Do: One block on a pane, set apart by its fill and corners.

examples.name: NestedSurfaces
examples.title: Don't: A surface in a surface in a surface: the fills stack up.

examples.name: NamedRegions
examples.title: Do: A heading that names each region.

examples.name: FillsOnly
examples.title: Don't: Regions told apart by their fills alone, which are close in contrast.

parts.description: A surface: fill, padding and corners.

components.name: List
components.summary: A vertical list of connected rows, each with a title, a detail and an action, that can open what it names, show the current one and be put in order.
useWhen: Related items with a title, a short detail and an action each, such as the sections of a settings page.
Items that each open a page or a document, such as recent plans (`interactive`).
A short set of results or members under a search field.
The list beside an item's details, with its current row marked (`selected`).
Items people put in their own order, such as the slides of a deck or an agenda (`onReorder`).

avoidWhen.text: Data compared across columns, or rows people sort by a value.
Destinations in an application's navigation.
A hierarchy people expand, such as folders.
One choice from a few options shown as rows.
Content about one subject that stands on its own.

examples.name: SettingsRows
examples.title: Settings rows
examples.description: A list is a column of connected rows, each with a label, a description and an action at its end.

examples.name: OpenFromRow
examples.title: Open from row
examples.description: With `interactive`, the link marked `data-row-target` covers its row. The row's other controls take `position: relative` to stay above it.

examples.name: CurrentRow
examples.title: Current row
examples.description: `selected` marks the row whose details show beside the list, with `aria-current`.

examples.name: CheckedRows
examples.title: Checked rows
examples.description: A checkbox in `start` chooses rows for an action on several at once.

examples.name: Reorder
examples.title: Reorder
examples.description: `onReorder` gives each row a handle: drag it, or press <kbd>Space</kbd> and move the row with the arrow keys. The list reports the move, and the application moves the item.

examples.name: OneTarget
examples.title: Do: One link per row, which covers the row.

examples.name: SeveralTargets
examples.title: Don't: Several links in a row: a press could open any of them.

examples.name: SameActions
examples.title: Do: The same kind of action at the end of every row.

examples.name: MixedActions
examples.title: Don't: A different action on each row: people can't scan them.

parts.description: The announcements of a reordered item.
The handle that reorders an item.
The start of an item, for the handle or a checkbox.
Rows joined into one block: lists and vertical radio groups.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A rounded surface that groups content about one subject, as a content card with a title and actions, a feature card, or one link or button.
useWhen: Content about one subject stands apart from the page, such as a project's summary.
A summary needs its own actions along the bottom, such as Share and Open (`actions`).
The whole surface leads to one destination or starts one action, such as a project in a grid (`href`, `onClick`).
A feature is introduced with an icon, a sentence and one action (`layout="feature"`).

avoidWhen.text: A fill, padding and corners without card semantics or spacing, such as a toolbar's background.
Rows of items with a label, a description and an action, connected in one list.
Data to compare across rows and columns.
A message about the page or a section.
A region with no content yet.

examples.name: ProjectSummary
examples.title: Project summary
examples.description: A card groups content about one subject on a rounded surface.

examples.name: ActionStrip
examples.title: Content card
examples.description: The default: `title`, `meta`, `description`, and `actions` in a strip along the bottom.

examples.name: FeatureCards
examples.title: Feature card
examples.description: `layout="feature"`: an icon, a title and a sentence, and one action.

examples.name: Destinations
examples.title: Link card
examples.description: With `href`, the whole card is one link.

examples.name: StartOptions
examples.title: Button card
examples.description: With `onClick`, the whole card is one button. It holds only phrasing content, such as spans.

examples.name: OneCardSections
examples.title: Do: One card per subject, with Text for its parts.

examples.name: NestedCards
examples.title: Don't: Cards inside cards: the fills and corners stack up.

examples.name: ShortCard
examples.title: Do: A short title that names the subject, and a sentence or two.

examples.name: WordyCard
examples.title: Don't: A long title and a paragraph: the card stops being scannable.

parts.description: The card's content above the footer.
The row with the title and the meta.
The icon of the feature layout.
The row of the feature layout: icon, text and actions.
The short fact at the end of the title row.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action, or goes to a destination with href, alone, icon-only, confirmed in place, copying a value or connected in a group.
useWhen: Someone starts an action, such as saving, creating or sending.
A prominent destination, such as the next step of a flow, should look like an action.
An icon alone names a familiar action in a dense place, such as a toolbar (IconButton).
An action takes effect at once and cannot be undone, such as removing someone's access (ConfirmButton).
People copy a value to paste elsewhere, such as a link, an ID or a command (CopyButton).
Related actions belong together, such as the main action and a menu of alternatives (ButtonGroup).

avoidWhen.text: A destination inside running text.
Choosing one of a few views or filters that stays selected.
A setting that turns on or off.
A list of actions that would crowd a toolbar.
A consequence that needs a choice or typed confirmation before it happens.

examples.name: CreateProject
examples.title: Create project
examples.description: A button starts an action. With `href` it is a native link that looks like a button.

examples.name: PendingAction
examples.title: Pending action
examples.description: While `pending`, a spinner replaces the content at the same size, and presses do nothing.

examples.name: ConfirmInPlace
examples.title: Confirm in place
examples.description: ConfirmButton arms on the first press and acts on the second. <kbd>Esc</kbd>, leaving it or 4 seconds disarm it.

examples.name: CopyValue
examples.title: Copy value
examples.description: CopyButton copies its `value` and shows Copied, or Couldn’t copy, for about two seconds.

examples.name: OnePrimaryAction
examples.title: Do: One primary button per group, at the end of its actions.

examples.name: SeveralPrimaryActions
examples.title: Don't: Several primary buttons: none of them stands out.

examples.name: ExplainWhatIsMissing
examples.title: Do: Let people press it, then show what is missing.

examples.name: DisabledUntilValid
examples.title: Don't: A disabled button that doesn’t say why.

examples.name: SpecificLabel
examples.title: Do: Name the action and what it affects.
examples.description: Start with a verb and say what will happen.

examples.name: VagueLabel
examples.title: Don't: OK or Submit, when a specific verb fits.

parts.description: The spinner of a pending button.
The button that shows only an icon.
The button that asks to confirm before acting.
The announcement of the confirming state.
The button that copies a value.
The field that shows the value beside the button.
The announcement that the value was copied.
The row or column of related buttons.
The surface of menus, popovers, tooltips and lists.
The theme boundary around a popup.

components.name: CloseButton
components.summary: The icon-only button that closes, dismisses or removes what it sits in, named Close in the application's language.
useWhen: A panel, a notification or a tip closes or is dismissed in place.
A list of items, such as people or files, lets each be removed.

avoidWhen.text: A dialog's own close, which Dialog renders itself.
An action that deletes something for good, which needs its consequence named.
Any other icon-only action.

examples.name: DismissTip
examples.title: Dismiss tip
examples.description: CloseButton is an icon-only button with a cross that closes, dismisses or removes what it sits in. Under a coarse pointer, its hit area reaches the 2.75 rem touch size.

examples.name: ApplicationLabel
examples.title: Application label
examples.description: `aria-label`, else EnvUIProvider's `messages.common.close`, else Close, in the language the provider sets.

examples.name: CloseAtEnd
examples.title: Do: At the end of the header of what it closes, where people look for it.

examples.name: CloseAtStart
examples.title: Don't: At the start: it reads as part of the content.

examples.name: OneClose
examples.title: Do: One way to close, beside the actions.

examples.name: TwoCloses
examples.title: Don't: A cross and a Close button: two ways to do one thing.

parts.description: The button that closes a dialog, panel or message.

components.name: SearchTrigger
components.summary: The button that opens search or a command palette, with its ⌘K or Ctrl+K shortcut, as a field-like row or an icon.
useWhen: Search or a command palette opens from a button at the top of a sidebar or in a header.
The application opens search with a keyboard shortcut and shows it where people look for search.
A narrow header or a sidebar showing icons only needs search as an icon.

avoidWhen.text: People type the search on the page itself and the results filter in place.
The search itself, with its field and results.

examples.name: InSidebar
examples.title: In sidebar
examples.description: SearchTrigger is the button that opens an application's search. It looks like a search field and presses itself on its shortcut, ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere, so `onClick` is the one place search opens.

examples.name: UsualShortcut
examples.title: Do: The platform's usual shortcut for search.

examples.name: EditorShortcut
examples.title: Don't: A shortcut that editors need, such as Ctrl+B for bold.

examples.name: ButtonLabel
examples.title: Do: Search, or what it searches where there are several.

examples.name: TypingLabel
examples.title: Don't: A placeholder's words: people expect to type, but it is a button.

parts.description: The tooltip of the icon-only button.
The surface of menus, popovers, tooltips and lists.
The theme boundary around a popup.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, one tab stop from the page, moved through with the arrow keys.
useWhen: A set of controls acts on one subject, such as an editor's formatting or a diagram's view.
Many icon-only actions sit together and would make a long tab sequence one by one.
A tool is chosen from a palette and stays chosen, such as a drawing tool.

avoidWhen.text: A form's or a dialog's actions, which keep a tab stop each.
Buttons joined into one connected control, such as a main action and its menu.
A choice of one view or filter, shown as a selected segment.
An application's menus of commands, such as File and Edit.
A page's search, filters and primary action, where fields keep their arrow keys.

examples.name: FormattingToolbar
examples.title: Formatting toolbar
examples.description: A toolbar holds the controls for one subject, such as an editor's formatting, as one tab stop that the arrow keys move through. `Toolbar.Button` is an icon button named by its `label`, which a tooltip shows with its `shortcut`; with `pressed` it is a toggle.

examples.name: PageToolbar
examples.title: Layouts
examples.description: Not every bar of controls is a Toolbar. examples.name: GroupedControls
examples.title: Do: Related controls in groups, with separators between them.

examples.name: UngroupedControls
examples.title: Don't: Controls in no order: people search the whole row.

examples.name: SameIconPressed
examples.title: Do: A toggle keeps its icon, pressed or not.

examples.name: IconSwapsPressed
examples.title: Don't: A pressed toggle that changes its icon: people lose track of what it does.

components.name: Link
components.summary: A destination inside running text, underlined by default, routed by the application.
useWhen: A destination inside a sentence or a paragraph, such as a guide or a related page.
A short list of destinations where buttons would be too heavy, with the underline turned off.

avoidWhen.text: An action, such as saving or deleting, even when it looks like text.
The next step of a flow, which should read as an action.
Destinations in an application's navigation, such as a sidebar.
Previous and next pages of a sequence.

examples.name: InRunningText
examples.title: In running text
examples.description: Link is a native `<a>` for a destination inside running text. It renders through the `LinkProvider`'s link component, so the application's router handles it.

examples.name: UnderlinedInText
examples.title: Do: The underline in running text.

examples.name: NoUnderlineInText
examples.title: Don't: No underline in a sentence: only its color tells it apart.

examples.name: NamesDestination
examples.title: Do: Words that name the destination.

examples.name: ClickHere
examples.title: Don't: Click here: it says nothing out of context.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: A color area, a hue slider and a HEX field for choosing an opaque color, and a color swatch that shows one.
useWhen: People choose any opaque color, such as an accent or a label's color, by eye or by its HEX value.
A button or a list shows a color that people chose, as a round sample (ColorSwatch).

avoidWhen.text: Choosing one of a few named colors or themes.
Choosing one of a fixed list of colors with names.
A light, dark or system appearance.

examples.name: AccentColor
examples.title: Accent color
examples.description: A color picker chooses an opaque color with a color area, a hue slider and a HEX field that stay in step.

examples.name: SwatchButton
examples.title: Swatch button
examples.description: In a Popover, opened by a button that shows the color as a swatch and its value.

examples.name: ProjectColorForm
examples.title: Project color form
examples.description: `name` submits the HEX value, and a reset returns to `defaultValue`.

examples.name: SwatchWithValue
examples.title: Do: A swatch with the color's value in text.

examples.name: SwatchAlone
examples.title: Don't: A swatch alone, which names no color.

examples.name: ContrastChecked
examples.title: Do: Check the contrast of a color that carries text, and say what is wrong.

examples.name: ContrastUnchecked
examples.title: Don't: A color too light for text, taken without a word.

parts.description: The area that holds the plane and the sliders.
The plane of saturation and lightness.
The announcement of the chosen color.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: Single-line inputs, search fields and multiline textareas share labels, guidance and states.
useWhen: Someone types a short value on one line, such as a name, an e-mail address or a number.
A value has a fixed start or a unit beside it, such as an address after a domain or a size in GB.
People search or filter a list, a table or a sidebar by typing (SearchField).
Someone writes text over several lines, such as a description or notes (Textarea).

avoidWhen.text: Text that runs over several lines.
A query that searches or filters content, which needs a search icon and a way to clear it.
Choosing one of a few known options.
Choosing from a long list of options by typing to filter them.
A date, or a date and time.
A time of day.
A month of a year.
A message in a conversation, sent with Enter.
Formatted text, such as headings, lists and links.

examples.name: ProjectName
examples.title: Project name
examples.description: A text field takes a short value on one line, with a label, a description and an error.

examples.name: LoadingPage

Rows people preview with a click and open to keep with a double click, as in a desktop editor.

avoidWhen.text: An application's destinations, such as the pages in a sidebar, one or two levels deep.

examples.name: FileTree

examples.name: ContextMenuActions
examples.title: Context menu actions
examples.description: With `contextMenu`, right click, a long press, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> or the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key open a menu for a row, or for the empty area. Offer the same actions in visible controls.

examples.name: GoToDocument
examples.title: Go to document
examples.description: A command palette is a search field over a list, near the top of the window, for jumping to anything by name. The application owns the items, how they are filtered and ranked, and what choosing one does.

examples.name: RunCommand
examples.title: Run command
examples.description: `end` holds a shortcut or a Badge; `hints` show the keys in the footer.

examples.name: ShowRecent

examples.name: EmptyUntilTyped
examples.title: Don't: An empty list until people type.

parts.description: The footer with the keyboard hints.
The row with the search input.
The message when nothing matches, and its announcement.
The row anatomy of menu, select and combobox options.
The end of a row, for a shortcut or a check.
The check of a chosen row.
The column with a row's label and description.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: Actions, destinations and the shared organization switcher, opened from a trigger or a right click.
useWhen: A short list of actions behind one control, such as a row's or a toolbar's More actions.
A few destinations that share a trigger, such as the account pages behind the avatar.
Options that change a view, such as a sort order or whether hidden files show, as radio and checkbox items.
Actions for an area or its rows on right click, beside the visible controls that offer them too (ContextMenu).
Switching between the organizations a person belongs to, in the application shell (OrganizationSwitcher).

avoidWhen.text: The signed-in person's menu, with its header and theme submenu.
Choosing a value for a form field.
An application menubar, such as File, Edit and View.
Searching for and running one of many commands.
An application's navigation, such as the pages in a sidebar.
Content people work in beside a trigger, such as a small form or a color picker.
Switching between views of the same content.
One or two actions that fit beside the content they act on.

examples.name: IconsAndShortcuts
examples.title: Icons and shortcuts
examples.description: A menu shows a short list of actions or destinations from one control, on a temporary surface. Menu.Root opens Menu.Item rows from its `trigger`, and the other parts build the rest.

examples.name: ContextMenuForRows
examples.title: Context menu for rows
examples.description: ContextMenu opens a menu for an area on right click, long press, the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>. Offer the same actions in a visible button too.

examples.name: AccountMenu
examples.title: Account menu
examples.description: An AvatarButton trigger and a Menu.Header with the account. The full menu, with the theme and the organizations, is the account menu pattern.

examples.name: SwitchOrganization
examples.title: Switch organization
examples.description: OrganizationSwitcher shows the active organization and switches between the person's organizations; `onCreate` adds the create action. It fits a navigation Drawer's `header`.

examples.name: FirstOrganization
examples.title: First organization
examples.description: Without organizations, the switcher is only the create action.

examples.name: GroupsAndSeparators
examples.title: Groups and separators
examples.description: Menu.Group puts items under a heading; Menu.Separator splits sets without one.

examples.name: Choices
examples.title: Radio and checkbox items
examples.description: A Menu.RadioItem checks one choice and closes the menu; a Menu.CheckboxItem toggles and keeps it open. ThemeRadioGroup is the theme choice as radio items.

examples.name: Submenus
examples.title: Submenus
examples.description: A Menu.Submenu row opens a nested menu beside it, on hover or with <kbd>→</kbd>.

examples.name: Destinations
examples.title: Destinations
examples.description: With `href`, an item is a link, through the `LinkProvider`.

examples.name: FrequentFirst
examples.title: Do: Frequent actions first, and a destructive one last, apart.

examples.name: DeleteFirst
examples.title: Don't: Delete first, where the keyboard lands.

examples.name: DisabledWithReason
examples.title: Do: Keep an unavailable item, disabled, with a description of why.

examples.name: HiddenItem
examples.title: Don't: An item that disappears, so people wonder where it went.

examples.name: ConsistentIcons
examples.title: Do: An icon on every item of a set, or on none.

examples.name: MixedIcons

components.name: Menubar
components.summary: A desktop-style menubar of menus, such as File, Edit and View, with shortcuts, submenus and access keys.
useWhen: A document-centred application has many commands, grouped as a desktop application groups them, such as File, Edit, View and Help.
A window draws its own title bar and holds the application's menus at its start (with TopBar's `titleBar`).

avoidWhen.text: A short list of actions behind one control.
Destinations in an application's navigation.
Running a command by name.
A row of actions that stay visible, such as a toolbar.

examples.name: NotesMenubar
examples.title: Notes menubar
examples.description: A menubar holds an application's commands as a desktop window does: a row of menus, such as File, Edit and View. After a command, focus returns to where it was, so Copy acts on the field people were in.

examples.name: InTitleBar
examples.title: In title bar
examples.description: A TopBar with `titleBar` holds the menubar at its start, as the window frame pattern shows.

examples.name: StandardOrder
examples.title: Do: Menus in the order people expect: File, Edit, View, your own, then Help.

examples.name: UnusualOrder
examples.title: Don't: Help first and File in the middle.

examples.name: LongMenuNames

parts.description: The underlined access key in a trigger's label.
A button that opens a menu.
The surface of menus, popovers, tooltips and lists.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short label beside a control on hover and keyboard focus, such as an icon-only button's name or why a control is disabled.
useWhen: Showing an icon-only control's name, such as a toolbar's Refresh button, for people who don't recognise the icon.
Saying why a control is disabled, such as All seats are assigned, beside the page's own account of it.
Showing a control's keyboard shortcut, such as Bold (Ctrl+B).

avoidWhen.text: A preview of a person, a page or an item, with more than a line of text, on hover or focus.
Content people interact with, such as a small form or a list of choices.
Guidance people need to fill in a field, such as a format or a limit.
Information people need that should stay visible, such as a warning about a limit.

examples.name: IconActions
examples.title: Icon actions
examples.description: A tooltip is a short label beside a control, shown while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus.

examples.name: MenuTrigger
examples.title: Menu trigger
examples.description: A Tooltip can be the `trigger` of a Menu.Root, Popover, Dialog, Sheet or ConfirmDialog, and stays closed while their popup is open.

examples.name: ShortcutHints
examples.title: Shortcut hints
examples.description: Write the shortcut after the name, and give the control `aria-keyshortcuts`.

examples.name: RepeatsLabel
examples.title: Don't: A tooltip that repeats a visible label.

examples.name: DisabledReason
examples.title: Do: Say why a control is disabled in the page too.

examples.name: ReasonOnlyInTooltip
examples.title: Don't: The reason only in a tooltip, which touch screens never show.

examples.name: ShortName
examples.title: Do: A few words, the same as the control’s accessible name.

examples.name: LongTooltip
examples.title: Don't: A paragraph people must hold the pointer still to read.

parts.description: The wrapper that lets a disabled control show a tooltip.

components.summary: A floating panel beside its trigger for details or a small form; Esc or a press outside closes it.
useWhen: Details about something on the page that people open on demand, such as a document's history or what a setting means.
A small form beside the control it changes, such as renaming an item or choosing filters.
An explanation behind an icon button, such as a help mark beside a value.

avoidWhen.text: A short name or hint for a control, shown on hover and focus.
A preview of a link's destination, shown on hover.
A list of actions or destinations.
Choosing a value for a form field from a list.
A task that needs people's full attention or more room, or a consequence to confirm.

examples.name: DocumentDetails
examples.title: Document details
examples.description: A popover is a floating panel beside its trigger, for details people ask for or a small form that changes something nearby. It takes focus as it opens and closes with <kbd>Esc</kbd>, a press outside or when focus leaves it; it isn't modal, so the page stays usable.

examples.name: RenameInPlace

examples.description: A function child receives `close`, to close the popover once its action is done.

examples.name: FilterTasks

examples.description: `open` and `onOpenChange` control the popover, here starting from the filters in use each time it opens.

examples.name: ShortHelp

examples.name: LongHelp

useWhen: A link or a name refers to something people may want a glance at before following it, such as a document's summary or a person's role.

avoidWhen.text: A short hint that names a control.
Details or a small form that people open on purpose and work in.
A task that needs people's attention before they go on.
Information people need to complete a task, which must stay visible.

examples.name: DocumentPreview

Several limits people compare at a glance, such as a plan's seats, projects and requests.

examples.name: SameWidths

examples.name: MixedWidths
examples.title: Don't: Bars of different lengths, side by side.

examples.name: StorageQuota

examples.name: PercentOfStorage

patterns.name: forms
patterns.title: Form layout and validation
patterns.summary: Ask for information in a form, check it, and help people fix what's wrong.
useWhen: Someone gives or changes several pieces of information at once, and submits them together.
A form refuses what people entered and they need to find and fix each problem.

avoidWhen.text: A single setting that takes effect at once.
Confirming a destructive action.
Filtering a list or a table as people choose.

examples.name: CreateProject
examples.title: Create project
examples.description: A form asks for information and gets it right on the first submit: one column of labelled fields, the primary action after the last, and errors that say how to fix each problem, with focus taken to where people need to act.

examples.name: ValidationTiming
examples.title: Validation timing
examples.description: On submit first: show each field's `error`, and move focus to the error summary, or straight to the field when there is only one. Then as people leave a field they have typed in. Never while they type, though an error goes as soon as the value is right.

examples.name: ServerError
examples.title: Server error
examples.description: The submit Button is `pending` while the form is sent: it keeps its size and ignores presses. When the server refuses or can't be reached, keep everything people entered, and move focus to an Alert at the top that says what to do.

examples.name: ErrorSummary
examples.title: Error summary
examples.description: After a refused submit, a danger Alert titled "There is a problem" lists each error as a Link that moves focus to its field. Leave it without `announce`, so it is read once, as it takes focus.

examples.name: GroupedChoices
examples.title: Grouped choices
examples.description: One choice of several is a RadioGroup; several are Checkboxes in a native `fieldset` whose `legend` names them.

examples.name: OneColumn
examples.title: Do: One column, read top to bottom, with the action after the last field.

examples.name: SideBySide
examples.title: Don't: Fields side by side: people miss the one beside their path.

examples.name: VisibleLabel
examples.title: Do: A label, and the format as a description that stays.

examples.name: PlaceholderLabel
examples.title: Don't: The placeholder as the label: it goes as people type.

patterns.name: settings
patterns.title: Settings
patterns.summary: Let people change how the application works for them, and see each change apply.
useWhen: Someone changes a preference that applies at once, such as a notification or the theme.
Someone edits a few related values that only make sense saved together, such as a profile.

avoidWhen.text: Several answers given once and submitted together, such as creating something.
A choice that filters or changes the view of the page people are on.

examples.name: ImmediateToggles
examples.title: Immediate toggles
examples.description: Use this pattern to let people change how the application behaves for them: notifications, privacy, appearance, their profile and the rare action that can't be undone. Each setting either applies the moment people change it or waits, with the settings it depends on, for a Save button, and the two never share a section.

examples.name: SaveSection
examples.title: Save a section
examples.description: A profile's fields depend on each other, so they wait for Save. The section marks its unsaved changes, and Cancel puts back what was saved.

examples.name: AppearanceChoice
examples.title: Appearance
examples.description: The theme applies the moment people choose it, through `useThemePreference`. The density only keeps the choice in the example: the application stores it and passes it to the root provider's `scale`, the app's one scale.

examples.name: DangerZone
examples.title: Danger zone
examples.description: Deleting the workspace can't be undone and affects everyone, so the dialog asks for its name. A confirmation with the wrong name keeps the dialog open and says what to enter.

patterns.name: destructive-actions
patterns.title: Confirmation and destructive actions
patterns.summary: Let people delete, remove or archive with as little friction as is safe, and undo or confirm by what is at stake.
useWhen: People delete, remove, archive or end something.
An action affects other people or can't be undone.

avoidWhen.text: A decision that needs fields or several choices, beyond a confirmation.
Reporting the outcome of an action that people can't change.

examples.name: UndoInstead
examples.title: Undo instead
examples.description: Use this pattern to choose how much friction a destructive action needs. Asking "Are you sure?" before everything trains people to confirm without reading. Act at once when the action can be undone, ask in place when little is at stake, and keep a dialog, and a typed name, for what can't be undone or reaches other people.

examples.name: ConfirmInPlace
examples.title: Confirm in place
examples.description: Removing an attachment is small and quick to redo, so the button asks in place: the first press says "Remove file?", the second removes it.

examples.name: ConfirmDelete
examples.title: Confirm from a menu
examples.description: "Delete document…" in a row's menu opens a ConfirmDialog that names the document. Cancel returns focus to the menu button; after the delete, focus moves to the next row's menu button.

examples.name: TypeToConfirm
examples.title: Type to confirm
examples.description: Deleting a project with all its documents can't be undone, so the dialog asks for the project's name. The confirm button stays enabled, and a wrong name keeps the dialog open with an error. Focus opens on Cancel; Enter in the field confirms as the button does.

examples.name: BulkDelete
examples.title: Bulk delete
examples.description: The count of the selection is in the button, the question and the confirm button. After the delete, the button has gone with the selection, so focus moves into the list.

patterns.name: feedback
patterns.title: Notifications and feedback
patterns.summary: Tell people what happened, what state things are in and what needs them, in the place and at the volume each message deserves.
useWhen: People need to know the outcome of something they did, or of work that ran in the background.
A page, a row or a destination has a state people should notice.

avoidWhen.text: A value that is wrong in a form.
Content that is loading.
A region with nothing to show.

examples.name: SaveConfirmation
examples.title: Save confirmation
examples.description: Use this pattern to choose where a message goes and how loudly it speaks. A message about a field belongs on the field, a condition of the page in an Alert on the page, the outcome of an action in a toast, and a state of a row or a destination in a Badge or a count beside it. Each is announced at most once, and only what needs people interrupts them.

examples.name: SectionAlert
examples.title: A condition of the page
examples.description: A read-only project says so in a warning Alert that stays while the condition lasts. It is read with the page, not announced, and it offers the one thing people can do. Once the request is sent, its button goes, so focus moves to the Alert, which reads its new text once: a warning Alert without `announce` has no role, so the change isn't announced as well.

examples.name: BackgroundTask
examples.title: Background work
examples.description: The export runs while people carry on. When it ends, a toast with a "Download" action reaches them, and the page keeps a link to the file.

examples.name: StatusInRows
examples.title: Status in rows
examples.description: Each project's status is a Badge in its row, in one tone per status, with its words carrying the meaning.

examples.name: UnreadCount
examples.title: Unread counts
examples.description: A CounterBadge on a navigation item says how many new items wait there; its label says what it counts.

patterns.name: loading
patterns.title: Loading
patterns.summary: Show that something is loading, in the place and shape of what is coming, without implying how long it takes.
useWhen: A page, a region or the result of an action takes long enough that people would notice.
Work with a measurable end, such as an upload, runs while people wait.

avoidWhen.text: Content that turned out empty, or that failed to load.
The application frame itself before the first page loads, which shows its own parts as skeletons.

examples.name: SkeletonList
examples.title: Skeleton list
examples.description: Here each team's projects load the first time it is chosen: skeletons in the shape of the rows stand in for them, once the load has taken 200 ms.

examples.name: PageProgress
examples.title: Page progress
examples.description: Choosing a page in the navigation starts loading it: the page on screen stays, and stays selected in the navigation, and after 200 ms the bar along the top bar's bottom edge shows the next one is on its way, named by `loadingLabel`. When the page arrives, the bar completes and fades, the navigation selects it, and focus moves to the Scaffold's body, which takes focus without being a tab stop, unless people have moved focus elsewhere in the meantime. The Scaffold sits in a box here, with `landmarks={false}` and a block size of its own; an application renders it at its root.

examples.name: RefreshInPlace
examples.title: Refresh in place
examples.description: The activity stays while it refreshes; a small Spinner beside its heading says it is updating.

examples.name: PendingButton
examples.title: Pending button
examples.description: The button that saves shows the work in progress; the outcome is announced once it is done.

examples.name: UploadProgress
examples.title: Upload progress
examples.description: Progress measures each file and says what has been sent, in megabytes.

patterns.name: empty-states
patterns.title: Empty states
patterns.summary: Show what a region holds when it has nothing to show, tell first use from no results, done and failed, and offer the one way on.
useWhen: A list, a table or a page has nothing to show, for any reason.
A search or filters match nothing.
Content failed to load, or people may not see it.

avoidWhen.text: Content that is still loading.
Reporting that an action, such as a save, failed.

examples.name: FirstUse
examples.title: First use
examples.description: Use this pattern when a region has nothing to show, to say why and what people can do. "Empty" has four causes, and each needs its own words and action: nothing exists yet, nothing matches, everything is done, or the content failed to load or isn't theirs to see. The state takes the place of the list or the table, under the toolbar that stays.

examples.name: NoResults
examples.title: No results
examples.description: The search and the status filter stay above the state, which names the query, and a count says how many match. Clear filters resets both and returns focus to the search.

examples.name: LoadFailed
examples.title: Load failed
examples.description: In place of the table, a danger state says the documents are safe and offers Try again. The heading and the page's action stay.

examples.name: NoAccess
examples.title: No access
examples.description: The project exists, but not for this person: the state says who to ask, and Request access sends the request.

examples.name: AllDone
examples.title: All done
examples.description: When the last review is approved, the queue says so plainly, with what comes next and no action.

patterns.name: navigation
patterns.title: Navigation
patterns.summary: Let people move between the places of an application, see where they are, and find their way back.
useWhen: An application has several places, and people move between them.
People need to see where they are, how they got there and how to go back up.

avoidWhen.text: Narrowing a long list or a table to the items people want.
Showing more of the page's content without leaving the page.
Moving between pages of one long list.

examples.name: PrimaryNavigation
examples.title: Primary navigation
examples.description: Navigation gives an application one way around and a clear sense of place: one primary navigation that marks the current page, a trail back up from deep pages, tabs only for views of one thing, and a quick way to open anything by name.

examples.name: Hierarchy
examples.title: Hierarchy
examples.description: The trail shows the levels above the page, each a link; the page itself is the last level and no link.

examples.name: ViewsOfOneThing
examples.title: Views of one thing
examples.description: Tabs switch the views of one project in place. Its settings are another page, so they are a link in the header's actions.

examples.name: QuickOpen
examples.title: Quick open
examples.description: Choosing a result opens it as a link would. Here the trigger takes `listen={false}`, so <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> stays with the catalogue's own search.

examples.name: ListAndDetail
examples.title: List and detail
examples.description: As narrow as a phone, the detail shows in place of the list, with a back button that names where it goes.

examples.name: TabsForViews
examples.title: Do: Tabs for the views of the one thing the page is about.

examples.name: TabsForPlaces
examples.title: Don't: Tabs for places of the application: they have no address of their own.

patterns.name: app-frame
patterns.title: App frame
patterns.summary: Frame an application's screens with a Scaffold, a TopBar and the same destinations as a Bar, a Rail or a Drawer, by the width of the window.
useWhen: An application has a handful of destinations people move between, and a page for each.

avoidWhen.text: A window that draws its own title bar, in an installed application.
Moving between views of one object, such as its overview and its activity.

examples.name: AppFrame
examples.title: App frame
examples.description: The app frame is one Scaffold at the application's root, around the router's outlet: a TopBar with the name, search and the account menu, one array of destinations, and the page in the body.

examples.name: MenuOnPhones
examples.title: A menu on phones
examples.description: With many destinations, or none with icons, `forms={{ compact: 'none' }}` hides the bar, and a menu button in the top bar opens the same Drawer in a Sheet.

examples.name: WithDetails
examples.title: Details beside the page
examples.description: Side content that is not navigation goes in a supporting pane of Panes, in the body.

examples.name: DestinationsInNavigation
examples.title: Do: Every destination in the navigation, and the page's own action in its header.

examples.name: DestinationsInTopBar
examples.title: Don't: More destinations in the top bar: people look for them in two places.

patterns.name: account-menu
patterns.title: Account menu
patterns.summary: Show who is signed in and give them their own things, such as account settings, the theme and Sign out, from their avatar.
useWhen: People sign in, and need their account settings, the theme and Sign out within reach on every page.

avoidWhen.text: The application's places, such as Projects and Settings.
Switching organizations from a control of its own, such as at the top of the navigation.

examples.name: AvatarMenu
examples.title: Avatar menu
examples.description: The account menu is a Menu opened from the person's AvatarButton at the end of the TopBar: a header with who is signed in, then their own things, ending with Sign out.

examples.name: WithOrganizations
examples.title: Organizations
examples.description: A submenu switches between the person's organizations; the header names the current one.

examples.name: RowTrigger
examples.title: A row at the foot of the navigation
examples.description: A ghost Button `fullWidth` with the avatar and the name, as wide as the drawer; the menu opens above it with `side="top"`.

examples.name: AvatarTrigger
examples.title: Do: The person's own avatar, named by their name, at the end of the top bar.

examples.name: GenericTrigger
examples.title: Don't: The same icon for everyone: nothing says who is signed in.

patterns.name: window-frame
patterns.title: Window frame
patterns.summary: Frame an installed application's window that draws its own title bar, with the title bar across the top and the content scrolling below it.
useWhen: An installed web app or a desktop shell draws its own title bar, with the window controls over the page.

avoidWhen.text: An application's screen in a browser tab, with its top bar and navigation.
A page's own title and actions.

examples.name: StartPageWindow
examples.title: Start page window
examples.description: The window frame is for an installed application that draws its own title bar: a Scaffold with `topBarSpan="full"` and `scroll="body"`, a TopBar with `titleBar` across the top, and the content scrolling below it, where the window controls never cover a scrollbar.

examples.name: WithMenubar
examples.title: A menubar in the title bar
examples.description: A Menubar in the TopBar's `start`, and a page whose header sticks at the top of the body.

examples.name: WithNavigation
examples.title: Navigation below the title bar
examples.description: The Scaffold's navigation runs below the title bar, which spans the window.

examples.name: QuietTitleBar
examples.title: Do: The title and the menubar, with empty space to drag the window by.

examples.name: CrowdedTitleBar
examples.title: Don't: The page's actions in the title bar: no room is left to drag the window.

patterns.name: filtering
patterns.title: Filtering and search
patterns.summary: Let people narrow a list or a table to what they want, see how many items match, and undo it in one step.
useWhen: A list or a table is long enough that people look for some of its items.
People narrow items by what they are, such as their status, owner or type.

avoidWhen.text: Opening a page, a project or a document by name from anywhere in the application.
Choosing values for a form people submit.
Putting a table's rows in order.

examples.name: SearchAndFilters
examples.title: Search and filters
examples.description: Use this pattern to help people find items in a long list or table: a search field and a few filters above the results, each applied as people choose it, a count of what matches, and one way to clear it all. When nothing matches, the page says what was asked for and offers to clear it.

examples.name: FilterPanel
examples.title: Filters in a popover
examples.description: A Filters button opens a popover of checkboxes in two groups, Type and Edited by; each box filters the documents at once, and the button counts the filters in use.

examples.name: ActiveFilters
examples.title: Filters in use
examples.description: Each filter in use is a token that removes it, with "Add filter" to choose another and "Clear filters" to remove them all. envUI has no removable token yet: each is a small secondary Button with a Close icon, named "Remove filter" and its text.

examples.name: NarrowFilters
examples.title: Narrow windows
examples.description: Where the example is compact, narrower than 37.5 rem, the Selects move into a Sheet opened by a Filters button, and the search stays in the toolbar. Narrow the window to see it.

patterns.name: data-tables
patterns.title: Data tables
patterns.summary: Show many records in rows and columns that people can sort, page through, select and act on, also on narrow screens.
useWhen: People compare records by several values, such as their owner, status and date.
People sort records, page through them, or act on several at once.

avoidWhen.text: Items with one or two values each, such as a list of documents and their editors.
Narrowing the rows to the ones people want.
Hierarchical items that open and close, such as folders.

examples.name: SortAndPaginate
examples.title: Sort and paginate
examples.description: Use this pattern to show records people compare, sort and act on: a table with a link to each record, sortable columns, numbers aligned to compare, a page of rows at a time, and selection that leads to actions on several rows. On a narrow screen, the rows stack and a control above the table sorts them.

examples.name: SelectAndBulkActions
examples.title: Select and act on several rows
examples.description: Selecting rows shows the bulk bar: the count, a Toolbar of icon buttons that name the count, and "Clear selection". Archive acts at once and offers Undo; Delete asks first. Focus moves to the header's checkbox once the selection has gone, and back to Delete when its confirmation is cancelled. The count is announced through a status that is always there.

examples.name: RowActions
examples.title: Row actions
examples.description: The project's name is the row's link, and its other actions wait in a menu named for the row. "Delete project…" opens a confirmation; after the delete, focus moves to the next row's menu button, and after the last, to the empty state's "Create project".

examples.name: EmptyAndLoading
examples.title: Loading and empty
examples.description: Choosing a team loads its projects: Skeleton rows in the table's shape after 200 ms, then the table, or, for a team with none, an EmptyState in its place with "Create project".

examples.name: NarrowTable
examples.title: Narrow table
examples.description: As narrow as a phone, the rows stack with each value's label, and a Select and an IconButton above the table sort them, at the size of the small rows.

patterns.name: progressive-disclosure
patterns.title: Progressive disclosure
patterns.summary: Show what most people need first, and keep the rest one step away, in the place and at the depth that fits it.
useWhen: A page has options, details or actions that most people don't need most of the time.
A term or a value needs an explanation that would clutter the page if always shown.

avoidWhen.text: Switching between views of the same content.
Moving between destinations of the application.
Information people need to complete a task, such as a required field or an error.

examples.name: AdvancedOptions
examples.title: Advanced options
examples.description: Use this pattern to keep a page about its main task while the rest stays within reach: advanced options behind a disclosure, the long tail of a list behind "Show all", the details of a row in a sheet, rare actions in a menu, and the meaning of a term in a popover. Choose the component by how deep the content goes and whether people must act on it, and never hide what a task needs.

examples.name: ShowMore
examples.title: Show all
examples.description: The list shows its five most recent items; "Show all 12" shows the rest, and pressing it again hides them. The button keeps its place and focus; its label becomes "Show fewer", and `aria-expanded` says which state it is in.

examples.name: DetailsInSheet
examples.title: Details in a sheet
examples.description: Each row opens its project's details in a Sheet over the list, so people keep their place; closing it returns focus to the row.

examples.name: OverflowActions
examples.title: Overflow actions
examples.description: Share and Edit stay visible; the actions used less often wait in a "More actions" menu.

examples.name: ExplainATerm
examples.title: Explain a term
examples.description: A help button opens a Popover with a short definition and a link. The icon-only download button has a Tooltip that repeats its name.

Alert.description: An inline banner for a page- or section-level message, in its tone. It stays a server component: its dismiss button is a CloseButton, a client leaf named in the provider's language.

props.name: tone
props.description: What the message means: info, success, warning or danger, for an error or a failure. Sets the tint, the border and the icon; info and success alerts are also status messages.

props.name: title
props.description: A short heading for the message, such as "Sync paused", above the message.

props.name: children
props.description: The message: what it means and what people can do.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the tone's icon; false shows none.

props.name: action
props.description: An action below the message, such as a Button or Link.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls it; the application removes the alert.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the dismiss button, also shown as its tooltip.

props.name: announce
props.description: The alert appeared because of something that just happened and should interrupt: warning and danger alerts take the alert role. Info and success alerts are always polite status messages.

AnimatedNumber.description: A number within text that rolls to its new value when it changes: up when it grows and down when it shrinks, so a count updated by other controls is noticed. The text is always the current value.

props.name: value
props.description: The number to show; when it changes, the new value rolls in, up as it grows, down as it shrinks.

props.name: formatValue
props.default: the number format of EnvUIProvider's locale, or else the browser's
props.description: Writes the value as text, such as a currency.

Avatar.description: A round picture of a person or organization, with the default person picture or initials as fallback.

props.name: name
props.description: Person or organization name: the accessible name of a named avatar, and the initials fallback.

props.name: src
props.description: Picture URL. The fallback shows while it loads and when it is missing or fails.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Shown without a picture: the default person picture, or initials (for example, for an organization).

props.name: hue
props.description: The fill behind the initials or the person picture. Without it, the name chooses one, the same for the same name everywhere; set it for an organization with a color of its own.

props.name: size
props.description: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem, lg 3 rem or xl 5.5 rem, such as for a profile page.

props.name: named
props.description: Names the avatar as an image by `name`. Without it, the avatar is hidden from assistive technology, for when text beside it already names the person.

AvatarButton.description: A person's avatar as a button, typically the account menu trigger in a topbar. A halo shows hover, press and an open menu, and the tooltip names the account.

props.name: name
props.description: The person's name: shown in the tooltip, and the accessible name unless aria-label is set.

props.name: description
props.description: A second tooltip line, such as the e-mail address of the signed-in account.

props.name: src
props.description: Picture URL; the default person picture shows without one.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Shown without a picture: the default person picture (default), or the initials of `name`.

props.name: size
props.description: The picture: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem or lg 3 rem, inside a slightly larger hit area, which grows to the touch height under a coarse pointer.

AvatarGroup.description: Overlapping avatars for a set of people, such as the members of a project, with a chip that counts the rest and lists them in its tooltip. A ring in the color of the surface below separates the avatars.

props.name: people
props.description: The people, in order. Pass a preview with total when there are many more.

props.name: max
props.description: The most avatars to show; the overflow chip after them counts the rest. All by default.

props.name: size
props.description: As Avatar: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem, lg 3 rem or xl 5.5 rem.

props.name: total
props.description: How many people there are in all, when people is only a preview of them.

props.name: onPersonClick
props.description: Makes every avatar a button with a name tooltip; receives the person pressed.

props.name: formatMore
props.description: Text for people beyond the list, in the overflow tooltip and the group's name. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.avatarGroup.more` for this group.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: The group's name from the number of people and their names, which end with formatMore's text for people counted in total but not listed, such as "3 people: Alex Morgan, Sam Lee, 1 more". It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.avatarGroup.label` for this group; aria-label replaces it.

Badge.description: A small pill label for a state, such as In progress, Blocked or Archived, or for neutral metadata, such as a plan or a count of seats.

props.name: tone
props.description: Meaning of the state; done is the purple of completed work. Neutral by default.

props.name: variant
props.description: soft tints the background, solid fills it with the tone, outline draws a border.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as a check mark; hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.description: The label: a state, a name or a category in a word or two. It stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis where the badge is wider than its container.

Bar.description: The navigation bar for compact windows, such as phones: up to five destinations side by side, each an icon above its label, at the bottom of the window. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination is a tab stop.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array Rail and Drawer take. Give the bar 3 to 5: past 5 it shows the first 4 and a More item that opens the rest in a menu. Groups don't show.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

Box.description: A plain block for what needs no row or column of its own: an inset (`padding`), a size container (`container`) or a named node. It sizes to its content and never paints.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<ul />}, or another component to lay out without a wrapper, such as a Surface: the primitive's attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "filters" or "summary", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`. A component's part class names its node instead.

props.name: container
props.description: Makes the element a size container of this name, for container queries on its inline size, such as container="filters" for `@container filters (width >= 37.5rem)`. A container is as wide as its context gives it, never as its content. container="env-window" makes the element a window of its own on purpose, such as a preview frame, whose content lays out at its window class; other `env-*` names are envUI's own.

props.name: padding
props.description: The inset on every side, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

Breadcrumbs.description: The path from the top level to the current page; earlier levels are links.

props.name: items
props.description: From the top level to the current page, which is last.

props.name: wrap
props.description: The trail wraps onto more lines when it runs out of room; true by default. False keeps it on one line, for a bar or header: the current page is cut short first, and earlier levels keep their width.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark; name each trail where a page has several.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the `nav` element.

Button.description: Starts an action, or goes to a destination with href, in one of five variants and three tones, with optional icons; icon-only with iconOnly. It renders a native button or link.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis: primary for the main action of a view, secondary and outline for the rest, ghost for an application's chrome, such as a toolbar, and text for a link-like action. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives where that variant takes its tone, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else primary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning: neutral for most actions; accent, on a primary button only, for a rare consequential action, with 0.5 rem corners; danger for an action that deletes or ends something. Secondary buttons are always neutral.

props.name: underline
props.description: Show an underline for the text variant; defaults to false.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, such as sm for an action in a table cell or lg for the main call to action of a page. Without it, the button takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. A button beside a field takes the field's size.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the width of the container, such as the actions of a narrow form stacked in a column. An icon-only button keeps its square size.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as an Add icon.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: A decorative icon after the label, such as a ChevronRight for a next step.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started by this button is running: a spinner replaces the content without changing the button's size, and the button reports busy and ignores activation until pending ends.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination, cannot be focused or followed, and reports aria-disabled.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The action's name, such as Delete draft, for an icon-only button.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the element is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Show only icon, in a square button that keeps its size; name it with aria-label.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon of an icon-only button.

ButtonGroup.description: Connected buttons keep their own outer corners and share the row inner radius.

props.name: orientation
props.description: A row of buttons, or a column in which every button is as wide as the group.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the container's width, such as a sidebar's: in a row, labelled buttons share the room the icon-only ones leave, which keep their square size, and a row of icon-only buttons shares it evenly; in a column, every button is as wide as the group.

Calendar.description: A month of days to choose one from, following the WAI-ARIA date picker grid: the arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month (with Shift, by year), Home and End to the week's ends, and Enter or Space chooses the day. Named with aria-label or aria-labelledby, it is a group around the month's grid.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The day an uncontrolled calendar starts with; none by default, which shows today's month.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the chosen day as YYYY-MM-DD.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest day that can be chosen, as YYYY-MM-DD; earlier days are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest day that can be chosen, as YYYY-MM-DD; later days are unavailable.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: The first day of each week, from 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday: by default the locale's, or Monday where the browser cannot tell.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the month and weekday names and the day numbers: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's. The days are always Gregorian, also in a locale with a calendar of its own.

props.name: previousMonthLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the previous month button.

props.name: nextMonthLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the next month button.

CalendarHeatmap.description: A calendar of daily values with weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, colored in steps of a tone. Each day names its date and value, shows them in a tooltip on hover and focus, and the grid is one tab stop that the arrow keys move through.

props.name: data
props.description: Values by day; days without an entry count as 0.

props.name: startDate
props.description: The first day shown, as YYYY-MM-DD; the earliest day in data by default.

props.name: endDate
props.description: The last day shown, as YYYY-MM-DD; the latest day in data by default.

props.name: levels
props.description: Color steps including the empty step, 2 to 10; 5 by default.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The value that takes the strongest color; the largest value shown by default.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: The lowest value of each color step above the empty one, in ascending order, such as quantiles of the data to color by rank. Up to nine; they replace levels and maxValue. A day below the first threshold shows as empty, and a first threshold of 0 or less colors days of 0 too.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: The first day of each week column: 0 for Sunday (default) or 1 for Monday.

props.name: tone
props.description: The tone the colors are mixed from: accent by default.

props.name: formatValue
props.default: the number format of EnvUIProvider's locale, or else the browser's
props.description: Text for a value.

props.name: formatDate
props.default: the weekday, day, month and year in the locale, such as Tue 14 Oct 2025
props.description: Text for a day's date, in its accessible name and the default tooltip.

props.name: formatTooltip
props.description: Tooltip content for a day; the date and value by default.

props.name: monthLabels
props.default: the locale's short month names, from Intl
props.description: Twelve month names above the weeks, from January.

props.name: weekdayLabels
props.default: the locale's short weekday names, from Intl
props.description: Seven weekday names beside the rows, from Sunday.

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: Legend text before the lightest color. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.calendarHeatmap.less`.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: Legend text after the strongest color. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.calendarHeatmap.more`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the grid of days, such as "Deployments in the last year"; this or aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of visible text that names the grid of days, such as a heading; this or aria-label.

Card.description: A rounded surface that groups content about one subject: a content card with an optional title row and actions, a feature card with an icon and an action, or one link or button.

props.name: background
