props.description: The text beside the status icon, such as "Could not deliver". It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.message.sending` and `.failed`.

props.name: children
props.description: The message. Plain text keeps its line breaks; formatted content, such as Markdown, fills the width of a message from someone else.

MessageList.description: The messages of a conversation in order, as a log: assistive technology politely announces messages added anywhere in it and text that changes. Set busy while a reply streams in or earlier messages load. Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: busy
props.description: Messages are still changing, such as a reply streaming in or earlier messages loading. The log reports aria-busy, so assistive technology can wait for the change to finish instead of announcing every step.

Meter.description: A measurement within a known range, such as the seats assigned of a plan or the storage used of a quota: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a meter. For how much of a task is done, use Progress.

props.name: value
props.description: The measurement, between min and max. A value outside the range shows, and is reported, as the nearest end.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it is visible above the bar and names it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

MonthPicker.description: A field for a month of a year that shows the value in the reader's locale and opens a year of months to choose it from, with keyboard access like Calendar's.

props.name: value
props.description: The value: a month as YYYY-MM. null, or an empty string, for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores; none by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the new value as YYYY-MM, or null once the field is cleared.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest month, as YYYY-MM; earlier months are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest month, as YYYY-MM; later months are unavailable.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown value and the month names: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's. Months are Gregorian, also in a locale with a calendar of its own.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the field shows the value: Intl.DateTimeFormat options, by default the long month and the year, in the Gregorian calendar unless they name another.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the field's clear button and text of the popup's.

props.name: thisMonthLabel
props.description: The popup's shortcut to the current month.

props.name: previousYearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the popup's previous year button.

props.name: nextYearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the popup's next year button.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's button, which shows the value and opens the popup.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the value is submitted under with a form.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is needed: an empty field keeps its form from submitting and takes focus.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The value can be read and focused but not changed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while the field is empty and its label floats or is hidden.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, at the control height, or floating, 3.5 rem tall with room for its label, for long forms on a page.

props.name: size
props.description: The field's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label inside the field, where it floats into the outline while the field has a value, focus or its popup open. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A clear button in the field and in the popup removes the value.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open; with `onOpenChange` it controls it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popup starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

OrganizationSwitcher.description: Shows the active organization and switches between the person's organizations; fits a top bar or the top of a navigation drawer.

props.name: items
props.description: Organizations the signed-in person belongs to, in display order.

props.name: value
props.description: The active organization's id, or null before one is chosen.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the id of the organization chosen, unless it is the active one; the application switches and reports progress.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Offers creating an organization at the end of the menu, or as the only action without organizations.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading inside the menu.

props.name: createLabel
props.description: Label of the create action.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Trigger text while no organization is active.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents opening, for example while a switch is in progress.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menu.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the menu popup, beside env-organization-switcher; ref and style go to the popup too. Without organizations there is no popup.

props.name: triggerClassName
props.description: Class of the trigger button, or of the create button without organizations.

props.name: ref
props.description: The menu popup's ref; the trigger is a Button of its own.

props.name: style
props.description: The menu popup's inline style.

Page.description: The column a page's content sits in: invisible structure that never paints, centered, as wide as `width` at most, with the page gutter at its edges and the page's header at its top. Its gutters follow the window class of the region it sits in, such as a Scaffold's body or a pane, and it is the env-page container for the content inside. It adds no landmark; put it in a Scaffold's body, or the application's own main.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the content may grow, a readable width: sm (40 rem) for a form or a settings page, md (60 rem) for a document or a detail page, lg (76 rem) for a dashboard or a list, full for content that uses the whole width, such as a board. The column is centered in the space it has.

props.name: header
props.description: The page's heading, usually a PageHeader, at the top of the same column.

props.name: gutter
props.description: Pads the column at its inline edges with the page gutter, which follows the window class of the region the page sits in: 1 rem in a compact one, 1.5 rem from medium. False leaves the edges to the content, such as a page that is one full-bleed table.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "settings", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<article />}; a div by default. The page's class and attributes merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The page's content, under its header.

PageHeader.description: The heading of a page: its title with an optional trail above it, a description, leading content, meta beside the title, actions at the end and a toolbar row under it, built from Row and Column. It responds to its own width, and can stick to the top of the area that scrolls.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's title. It wraps, balanced across its lines, and is never cut short.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level: 1 for the page's own heading, a lower level for a header inside a pane or a section that sits under another heading. It looks the same at every level.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, in the smaller muted text, such as what the page is for.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: The trail to the page, usually Breadcrumbs with wrap={false}, above the title.

props.name: start
props.description: Before the title: an Avatar, an icon or a back IconButton.

props.name: meta
props.description: Beside the title, wrapping with it: Badges, such as a status, or a count.

props.name: actions
props.description: The page's actions, at the end of the title row: its primary action last. Below 37.5 rem of the header's own width, a compact one, they move under the title and wrap.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: A second row under the title: search, filters and view switches, laid out with `<Row wrap justify="between">`; see Toolbar's layouts.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keeps the header in view at the top of the area that scrolls, over the content that scrolls under it: under a Scaffold's top bar where the document scrolls, or at the top of a Scaffold's body that scrolls. As a Page's header, what scrolls into view below it, such as a field taking focus, keeps clear of it: the header measures its height, which CSS reckons from its rows until script runs.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: The size of the buttons and icon buttons in `actions` and `toolbar` that set none: sm for a dense page, such as one in a small window, or md. Give fields in the toolbar the same `size`.

Pager.Next.description: The destination after this one: a native link with rel="next", its title under the label Up next (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.next), and an optional icon after them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

Pager.Previous.description: The destination before this one: a native link with rel="prev", its title under the label Previous (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.previous), and an optional icon before them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

Pager.Root.description: A centered pair of previous and next destinations in a navigation landmark, from the previous and next props or from Pager.Previous and Pager.Next children; either one can be left out, and without any it renders nothing.

props.name: previous
props.description: The destination before this page, as the props of Pager.Previous; leave it out, or pass null, on the first page of a sequence.

props.name: next
props.description: The destination after this page, as the props of Pager.Next; leave it out, or pass null, on the last page of a sequence.

props.name: children
props.description: Pager.Previous and Pager.Next, instead of the previous and next props or beside one of them: they render between the previous prop's link and the next prop's, so the links keep their order.

props.name: aria-label
props.default: 'Previous and next content', or EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name; give each pager its own where a page has several.

Pagination.description: A compact pager for toolbars: the range of items shown, such as 1–60 of 245, and icon buttons for the previous and next pages, in a navigation landmark. The application loads the pages; the range is announced as it changes, and focus stays on the button pressed.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown, counted from 1. It is kept within the pages that exist, so a page beyond the end shows the last one.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: The most items a page shows, such as 60; at least 1.

props.name: total
props.description: All items, when known; the range then ends with it, as in 1–60 of 245, and the last page ends the list. Leave it out for a list read in batches, where hasNextPage says when it ends.

props.name: hasNextPage
props.description: Whether a later page exists, for a list without total, such as from a cursor's has more.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Receives the page before or after the current one when its button is pressed. The application loads that page and passes it back as page.

props.name: pending
props.description: A page is loading: the button pressed shows a spinner, also when the load starts in an effect after the page changes, and both buttons ignore presses while staying focusable. A load for another reason, such as a refresh, makes both wait without a spinner.

props.name: hideWhenSinglePage
props.description: Render nothing while every item fits on one page, so neither button has anywhere to go.

props.name: formatRange
props.default: 1–60 of 245, or 61–120 without total, with numbers in the locale
props.description: Writes the range from the first and last item shown, the total, the page and the page count, for one pager; EnvUIProvider's messages.pagination.range writes it for every pager.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: variant
props.description: The buttons' variant, as on IconButton, such as text for a quiet toolbar.

props.name: size
props.description: The buttons' height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, they take the control height of the container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name, such as Report pages, where a page has more than one.

PanelDock.Header.description: The header of a docked panel. It sticks to the top of the panel while its content scrolls: the title and its metadata at the start, the application's actions and the window controls at the end, small like a title bar's.

props.name: title
props.description: The panel's title, as a heading in 1.125 rem medium-weight text; it wraps between words rather than truncating.

props.name: meta
props.description: Supporting text below the title, in 0.875 rem muted text, such as who changed it last.

props.name: actions
props.description: The application's own actions, before the window controls, such as an Edit IconButton and a Menu of more; buttons that set no variant take the window controls' ghost one.

props.name: controls
props.description: Shows the window controls, Minimize, Maximize or Restore, and Close, inside a PanelDock; false leaves them out. EnvUIProvider's messages.panelDock names them.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level in the page outline; the look stays the same.

props.name: children
props.description: Content below the title row that stays with the sticky header, such as Tabs.

PanelDock.Root.description: Panels docked to the bottom inline-end edge of a region, beside the page, for items people work on alongside it, such as drafts and conversations: open panels side by side, one maximized panel filling the region, and minimized panels as tabs. A panel's content stays mounted through every change of mode and order.

props.name: panels
props.description: The panels in order, each a PanelDockPanel: open panels sit side by side, the newest at the end, and tabs follow in the same order. The application owns them.

props.name: children
props.description: Renders a panel's content from its panel, such as a PanelDock.Header above the panel's body. The content mounts once and stays mounted until the panel closes.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Called with the mode a panel asks for, from its window controls and its tab, and from the dock itself with overflow="minimize".

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called from a panel's close control and its tab's close button.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called when people press or focus inside a panel that is not active, and when its tab brings it back.

props.name: onHeightChange
props.description: Called with a panel's new height in pixels when a drag on its top edge ends, and on each key press there.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: A width, 40rem by default, or a number of pixels, such as 600 or "600": while the dock itself is narrower, one panel at a time fills it and the others wait as tabs. The dock then has data-stacked.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the dock stacks and with false when its panels sit side by side.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What the dock does when its open panels cannot all sit side by side at their minimum widths: scroll (default) scrolls the row sideways; minimize asks onModeChange to minimize the least recently active open panel, one at a time, until the rest fit, and to open it again once the region widens and it fits. It never asks for the active panel, the newest one or the one that holds focus, so never for a panel alone in the row, and where those cannot fit by themselves the row scrolls instead.

props.name: minimizedLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the list of tabs, which holds minimized panels and the panels a stacked dock leaves out, for this dock only.

props.name: openLabel
props.default: Show and the text, such as Show Budget, or EnvUIProvider's messages.panelDock.show
props.description: Accessible name of a tab's button that opens its panel, from the tab's text, for this dock only. A function, as each tab names its own panel.

props.name: closeLabel
props.default: Close and the text, such as Close Budget, or EnvUIProvider's messages.panelDock.closePanel
props.description: Accessible name of a tab's close button, from the tab's text, for this dock only.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.default: Resize and the title, such as Resize Quarterly report, or EnvUIProvider's messages.panelDock.resize
props.description: Accessible name of a panel's resize handle, from its title, for this dock only.

Panes.Detail.description: The detail pane of list-detail Panes, at the end. Below `splitAt` it shows only while `open`, with a back button to the list at its start, and focus follows what shows: the back button as the detail opens, the list's current row as it closes.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane, which makes it a region landmark that people can jump to, such as Documents. Name the panes of a page's main layout; leave small panes unnamed.

Panes.Divider.description: The divider between the panes, which resizes the supporting pane or the list: a focusable separator that the pointer drags and the arrow keys move, 1 rem a step, 5 with Shift, which names the pane it resizes in aria-controls. A double click returns it to the default width. It shows only while the panes sit side by side, and measures nothing until it is dragged.

props.name: label
props.description: The divider's name, which says what it resizes, such as Resize project list.

Panes.List.description: The list pane of list-detail Panes, at the start. Below `splitAt` it hides while `open`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane's region, such as Details or Projects.

Panes.Main.description: The main pane of supporting Panes, at the start.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane, which makes it a region landmark that people can jump to, such as Documents. Name the panes of a page's main layout; leave small panes unnamed.

Panes.Root.description: Two panes side by side, after Material's pane patterns, and how they behave in less room: a main pane with a supporting pane that becomes a sheet over it, or a list and its detail, one at a time. Invisible structure that never paints, except the supporting pane while it is a sheet, which is modal. Its own width decides, in CSS: it is the env-panes container. Each pane scrolls on its own when Panes has a height, as in a Scaffold's body that scrolls; an optional Panes.Divider resizes them.

props.name: behavior
props.description: supporting: Panes.Main and Panes.Supporting, such as a document and its details; below `splitAt` the supporting pane is a sheet over the main one while `open`. list-detail: Panes.List and Panes.Detail, such as messages and the one chosen; below `splitAt` one shows at a time, the detail while `open`, with a back button to the list.

props.name: splitAt
props.description: The window class of the Panes' own width from which the panes sit side by side: medium (37.5 rem), expanded (52.5 rem) or large (75 rem). Narrower, they behave as `behavior` says. CSS decides it, so the server's markup is right before any script runs.

props.name: open
props.description: Below `splitAt`: whether the supporting sheet is open, or the detail shows instead of the list. Side by side, both panes show whatever it is. The application keeps it, as it knows when an item is chosen or the sheet's button pressed.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with false when people close what `open` shows below `splitAt`: Escape, the close button or a press on the scrim closes the supporting sheet, and the back button returns from the detail to the list. Set `open` from it.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The name of the supporting sheet's close button, which shows only while the pane is a sheet.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The back button's label in a list-detail's detail, below `splitAt`. Name where it goes, such as All projects.

props.name: size
props.description: The resized pane's width in rem, for Panes the application controls with onSizeChange: the supporting pane, or the list. It applies while the panes sit side by side.

props.name: defaultSize
props.description: The resized pane's width in rem until people choose one with Panes.Divider, or one is kept under `persist`, and the width a double click on the divider returns it to.

props.name: onSizeChange
props.description: Receives each new width of the resized pane, in rem: while dragging the divider with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves it or a double click resets it.

props.name: minSize
props.description: The resized pane's smallest width, in rem.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The resized pane's largest width, in rem. It never leaves the other pane less than 16 rem.

props.name: persist
props.description: Keeps the width people choose in a cookie of this name, for Panes the application doesn't control; a double click on the divider forgets it and returns to `defaultSize`. Read it on the server with `readPanesSize(cookieHeader, key)` and pass it as `persistedSize`, so the server's markup has it and nothing moves as the page hydrates. Without that, the kept width applies after the first render.

props.name: persistedSize
props.description: The width kept under `persist`, in rem, as the server read it from the request's cookies with `readPanesSize`: the first render uses it, on the server and in the browser alike.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "inbox", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: children
props.description: The panes: Panes.Main, an optional Panes.Divider and Panes.Supporting; or Panes.List, an optional Panes.Divider and Panes.Detail.

Panes.Supporting.description: The supporting pane, at the end, such as details or filters for the main pane. Below `splitAt` it is a modal sheet over the main pane while `open`: a side sheet in a medium width, a bottom sheet in a compact one. Inside a Scaffold whose document scrolls, the sheet is the window's, as Sheet is: fixed to the window over a scrim, scrolling inside itself while the page stays. As a sheet it is a modal dialog with a close button: everything else on the page is inert, focus moves into it and Tab stays in it, and Escape, the close button or a press on the scrim closes it, which returns focus to where it was.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane's region, such as Details or Projects.

Popover.description: A floating panel beside its trigger, for details or a small form: it opens on press, moves focus into itself, and closes with Esc, a press outside or when focus leaves it. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the popover's surface.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens and closes the popover, such as a Button or an IconButton. It must take a ref and props: it receives the press handler, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

props.name: title
props.description: A heading at the top, such as the name of what the popover describes; it names the popover.

props.name: children
props.description: The popover's content, or a function that receives close, for an action inside it that should close the popover once it is done, such as a form's submit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The popover's accessible name when it has no title, such as Rename document.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the trigger the popover opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. It flips to the other side without room.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popover lines up with the trigger along that side: its start, center or end.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether a controlled popover is open; update it from onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popover starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state, and why, each time the popover asks to open or close: from the trigger, Esc, a press outside, focus leaving it or close (`close-press`).

props.name: width
props.description: The widest the popover grows: md, 20 rem, for details and a field or two; lg, 28 rem, for a longer form. It is as wide as its content from 12 rem up, and narrows to fit the window.

Progress.description: How much of a task is done, such as an upload or an import: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a progress bar. Pass value null while the amount of work is unknown, and the bar sweeps instead.

props.name: value
props.description: How much of the task is done, between min and max, such as 40 of 100; null while the amount of work is unknown, which shows an indeterminate bar announced as Loading.

props.name: segments
props.description: Splits the track into this many equal steps, such as 4 for a task of four stages, each filling in turn. Without it, the track is one bar.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it is visible above the bar and names it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

Radio.description: One option of a RadioGroup: a native radio input with its label, and an optional description.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native radio input, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The option's class, on its root element, the label around the radio and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the group reports and a form submits when this option is chosen.

props.name: label
props.description: The option's visible name, such as Private; pressing it chooses the option.

props.name: description
props.description: A short, muted line under the label that helps people choose, such as Only the people you invite. It is part of the option's label, so it is read with its name.

RadioGroup.description: A set of options to choose exactly one from: a native fieldset whose legend names the group, with Radio options inline or as selectable rows.

props.name: ref
props.description: The group's fieldset.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible name, such as Visibility, as the fieldset's legend above the options. It names the group for assistive technology; without it, use aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the chosen option in a controlled group; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value of the option an uncontrolled group starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without value or defaultValue, no option is chosen until people choose one.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: name
props.description: The name every radio of the group submits its value under. Set it in a form; without it the group takes a unique generated name, so its radios still work as one group.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits, through native constraint validation.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How the options are laid out: horizontal, radios before their labels side by side that wrap onto more lines; or vertical, connected selectable rows that fill the width, with the label and description at the start and the radio at the end, for options that need explaining.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every option of the group; a disabled group can't be focused or changed.

Rail.description: The navigation rail for medium windows, such as tablets: a narrow column at the window's start with the destinations one under another, each an icon above a short label. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination is a tab stop.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array Bar and Drawer take, each an icon above a short label. Groups don't show: the destinations follow one another in the array's order.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the destinations, such as a button that opens a Sheet with the Drawer, or the main action of the page.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content at the bottom of the rail, such as the account's AvatarButton.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

Rating.description: A read-only rating, such as a review score: stars filled to the value in half steps in the warning tone, with an optional number before them, named once for assistive technology as an image, such as "4.5 out of 5 stars". It shows a rating; it does not ask for one.

props.name: value
props.description: The rating, from 0 to max, such as 4.5. It shows rounded to the nearest half star, kept within 0 and max; a value that is not a number, such as NaN, shows no stars filled.

props.name: max
props.description: How many stars the scale has, as a whole number, such as 10. A fraction rounds to the nearest whole star; a value below 1 or not a number shows 5 stars.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the rating as a number before the stars, such as 4.5, in tabular digits and the locale's number format, such as 4,5 in German. The number is the rounded value the stars show, and it is hidden from assistive technology, since the stars' name already says it.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: Writes the accessible name of the stars from the shown value, rounded to a half star, and the number of stars. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.rating.label`, which receives both as text in the locale's number format.

RelativeTime.description: A moment in a time element as text relative to now, such as "3 hours ago", with the date and time in a tooltip. One shared clock keeps every RelativeTime on the page current.

props.name: value
props.description: The moment to describe: a Date, milliseconds since 1970 or a date string such as an ISO 8601 timestamp. An invalid moment renders nothing.

props.name: now
props.description: A fixed moment to compare with, for tests and server rendering; the text then stays as it is. Without it, or with an invalid one, the text follows the current time.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Show the date and time in a tooltip on hover, such as "Oct 14, 2026, 9:41 AM", in the reader's time zone and the locale. Turn it off where the exact moment shows nearby. Inside an application's own Tooltip, that one describes the time instead.

props.name: locale
props.default: EnvUIProvider's locale for RelativeTime, else the runtime's language: the browser's, or the server's while rendering there
props.description: The language of the text, and of the date and time in RelativeTime's tooltip, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en-GB" or "de", or a list of them in order of preference.

props.name: format
props.description: How long the words are, from Intl.RelativeTimeFormat: long "3 hours ago", short "3 hr. ago" or narrow "3h ago", in the locale's own wording.

props.name: nowLabel
props.default: 'just now' or 'now' in English, the locale's word for now elsewhere
props.description: Text for a moment less than 45 seconds away, past or coming, such as "moments ago". English says "just now" of a past moment and "now" of a coming one; other languages the locale's word. RelativeTime takes EnvUIProvider's `messages.relativeTime.now` without it.

RichText.description: Saved rich text, read-only: Markdown rendered with the editor's own schema and parser, so it shows what RichTextEditor wrote, references included, with envUI's links, code and checkboxes. It renders on the server too.

props.name: children
props.description: The Markdown to show, such as what RichTextEditor saved.

props.name: extensions
props.description: Tiptap extensions added to the shared schema, such as a custom mark. They must parse and write Markdown, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope; a new array starts a new editing session. Pass the same extensions to RichText.

props.name: renderReference
props.type: (reference: RichTextReference, context: { readOnly: boolean; selected: boolean }) => ReactNode
props.default: the trigger and the label, such as #Launch
props.description: Renders a reference's content, such as an avatar beside the name; it receives whether the document is read-only and whether the reference is selected.

props.name: onReferenceClick
props.description: Called when people activate a reference, with the reference and the event, such as to open the record. A reference with an href is a link, which the editor never follows while it is editable; without an href, this makes the reference a button.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Called when people activate a link in the document, with its href and the event: a native MouseEvent in the editor, a React mouse event in RichText. The editor never follows links while editable; call preventDefault to keep RichText or a read-only editor from following it.

RichTextEditor.description: A labelled editor for formatted text that people edit as it looks, built on Tiptap, with a formatting toolbar, references typed with a trigger such as

props.name: ref
props.description: Gives the Tiptap editor, as ref.current.editor, for commands.

props.name: value
props.description: The Markdown of a controlled editor; update it from onValueChange. A new value from outside, such as another draft, replaces the document and keeps the caret where it can.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The Markdown an uncontrolled editor starts with, and returns to when its form resets.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the document as Markdown after every edit, normalized by the editor's schema, so it can differ from the Markdown it was given, such as * for _ around italics.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the Markdown with a native form under this name, through a hidden input.

props.name: form
props.description: The ID of the form the hidden input belongs to, where the editor sits outside it.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown in an empty document, such as what to write.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Makes the editor unavailable: it cannot be edited or focused, the toolbar is disabled, its value is left out of form submission and it takes the shared disabled opacity.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the document without editing it: the toolbar is disabled and the document cannot be focused, but its links and references can, and the form still submits its value.

props.name: toolbar
props.default: every command, from heading to table
props.description: The toolbar's commands, in order, or false for no toolbar; Undo and Redo, and Attach files with onUpload, follow them.

props.name: references
props.description: Kinds of references people insert by typing a trigger, such as @ for people and # for topics, each with its own lookup. Triggers must be unique, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope.

props.name: slashCommands
props.description: Typing / opens a menu of block commands: true offers heading, the lists, quote, code block and table; an array adds the application's commands after them. A / reference source can't be used beside it.

props.name: onRequestLink
props.description: Opens the application's own link picker for Insert link, with the selected text, instead of the built-in dialog. Return the link, null to cancel, or a promise of either. A selection becomes a link to its href; at the caret, the label is inserted as the link's text.

props.name: onUpload
props.type: (file: File, request: { signal: AbortSignal }) => RichTextAttachment | null | Promise<RichTextAttachment | null>
props.description: Uploads a file people chose with Attach files, which shows in the toolbar only with this. Return where it lives as an attachment, null to skip it, or a promise of either; the signal aborts when the editor becomes read-only or disabled, or when a controlled value changes.

props.name: accept
props.description: The file types Attach files offers, as in a file input's accept, such as "image/*,.pdf".

props.name: multiple
props.description: Lets people choose several files at once with Attach files.

props.name: variant
props.description: The document's look, as a text area's: outline, in a bordered box on the field background; underline, without a border or fill, with an underline while it has focus; or ghost, only its text at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while it has focus. The document is always tall, with its label above it, so it has no floating variant.

props.name: extensions
props.description: Tiptap extensions added to the shared schema, such as a custom mark. They must parse and write Markdown, and the array must stay the same between renders, such as at module scope; a new array starts a new editing session. Pass the same extensions to RichText.

props.name: renderReference
props.type: (reference: RichTextReference, context: { readOnly: boolean; selected: boolean }) => ReactNode
props.default: the trigger and the label, such as #Launch
props.description: Renders a reference's content, such as an avatar beside the name; it receives whether the document is read-only and whether the reference is selected.

props.name: onReferenceClick
props.description: Called when people activate a reference, with the reference and the event, such as to open the record. A reference with an href is a link, which the editor never follows while it is editable; without an href, this makes the reference a button.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Called when people activate a link in the document, with its href and the event: a native MouseEvent in the editor, a React mouse event in RichText. The editor never follows links while editable; call preventDefault to keep RichText or a read-only editor from following it.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Row.description: Lays its direct children out side by side, `gap` apart, with `wrap` to run onto more lines, such as a form's actions. A flex row that sizes to its content and never paints.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets the row run onto more lines when its children don't fit, as a row of actions does.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between the direct children, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

props.name: align
props.description: How the children line up across the line: stretch, the default, makes each as wide as a column or as tall as a row, except controls such as buttons, which keep their own size; start, center and end keep every child at its own size.

props.name: justify
props.description: Where the children sit along the line when there is room to spare: at the start, in the center, at the end, such as a form's actions, or between, spread out to the edges.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<ul />}, or another component to lay out without a wrapper, such as a Surface: the primitive's attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "filters" or "summary", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`. A component's part class names its node instead.

props.name: container
props.description: Makes the element a size container of this name, for container queries on its inline size, such as container="filters" for `@container filters (width >= 37.5rem)`. A container is as wide as its context gives it, never as its content. container="env-window" makes the element a window of its own on purpose, such as a preview frame, whose content lays out at its window class; other `env-*` names are envUI's own.

props.name: padding
props.description: The inset on every side, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

Scaffold.description: The invisible structure of an application's screen, after Material's: a top bar region, a navigation region and the body. It never paints. It shows one navigation form at a time by its own width, CSS only: a Bar at the bottom of a compact window, a Rail at the start of a medium one and a Drawer at the start from expanded. The document scrolls by default, with the top bar, the bar and the rail or the drawer kept in view; `scroll="body"` scrolls the body alone. Skip links to the body and the navigation come first.

props.name: topBar
props.description: The top bar region, above the body: usually a TopBar.

props.name: navigation
props.description: The navigation forms, such as `{ bar: <Bar … />, rail: <Rail … />, drawer: <Drawer … /> }` with the same destinations. One shows at a time, chosen by the Scaffold's own width; give only the forms the application uses.

props.name: forms
props.description: Which form shows at each window class, or none, such as `{ compact: 'none' }` for an application that opens its navigation from the top bar on a phone. Where the form a window class asks for wasn't given, the nearest given form shows: a rail for a drawer and the other way round, then the bar.

props.name: topBarSpan
props.description: body: the top bar sits above the body, beside the rail or drawer, which run the full height. full: the top bar runs across the whole width, above the navigation, as a window's title bar must.

props.name: scroll
props.description: What scrolls. document: the page, as on any website, so a phone collapses its address bar, pull to refresh and a tap on the status bar work and the browser restores the scroll position; the top bar and the bar stick to the window's edges and the rail or the drawer stays in view, in a Scaffold at least as tall as the window. body: the body alone, under the top bar, in a Scaffold that fills its container's height, 100dvh unless a class gives it another, with the keyboard scrolling the body as it would the document: for a preview or an embedded frame, a window with its own title bar, or a body of Panes whose panes scroll on their own.

props.name: bodyId
props.default: 'main', or an id of its own where `landmarks` is false
props.description: The body's id, the target of the skip link to the content.

props.name: bodyRef
props.description: The body's element: with `scroll="body"` the element that scrolls, to read or restore its scroll position on.

props.name: skipLabel
props.description: The name of the skip link to the body.

props.name: skipNavigationLabel
props.description: The name of the skip link to the navigation.

props.name: landmarks
props.description: false renders the regions without landmarks, a div for the banner and the main, and no skip links, for a preview of an application inside another page's main content.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "app", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: children
props.description: The body: the page's main content, usually a Page or Panes.

SearchField.description: A search input with a search icon and, while it has a query, a clear button; Esc also clears. Its label is hidden by default, so it sits beside buttons with a placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's accessible name, such as Search members. It shows as a floating label only with showLabel; otherwise a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, as TextField does. A search field leaves it out, so that it sits in a toolbar with a placeholder such as Search.

props.name: value
props.description: The query of a controlled field; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The query an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the next query as people type, and an empty string when the clear button or Esc clears it.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The accessible name and tooltip of the clear button.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another, as a table cell does. A button beside a field takes the field's size. Floating and underline fields have their own height.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, with a thin border, at the control height; floating, an outlined field 3.5 rem tall whose label rests inside and floats into the outline, for long forms on a page; underline, as tall, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or ghost, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

SearchTrigger.description: The button that opens search or a command palette: a field-like button with its label and the shortcut's keys, or a search icon alone. It presses itself when the shortcut is pressed, and the application opens the search from onClick.

props.name: label
props.description: The label, and the name of the icon-only trigger.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keyboard shortcut, shown as keys at the end and announced as aria-keyshortcuts: `mod+k` is ⌘K on Apple platforms and Ctrl+K elsewhere. false shows and handles none.

props.name: listen
props.description: Press the trigger when the shortcut is pressed anywhere in the window, text fields included. With several triggers listening for one shortcut, the most recently mounted one that is visible and not behind a modal dialog takes it. A disabled trigger, or a key press that something else already handled, such as an editor's own shortcut, leaves the key alone.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Show only the search icon, in a ghost IconButton with the label and shortcut in a tooltip.

props.name: tooltipSide
props.description: The side of the trigger the icon-only tooltip opens on.

props.name: size
props.default: the container's control height, md unless the container sets another
props.description: The height, as on every control.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the width of the container, such as at the top of a navigation drawer.

SegmentedControl.description: One choice among a few items on a pill rail, such as views or filters of the same content; the chosen item takes the primary colors. A radio group, with one tab stop and arrow keys.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, two to five, in the order they show.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen item's value. The control is always controlled: update it from onValueChange.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the item people choose, by pressing it or with the arrow keys.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The group's accessible name, such as Work items; the control has no visible label.

props.name: size
props.description: The rail's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, so it lines up with buttons and fields of the same size. Without it, the rail takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the available width, split evenly between the items; a label too long for its share is cut short with an ellipsis and shows whole in a tooltip. Without it the control is as wide as its items, and scrolls in a container too narrow for them.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every item; the control can't be focused or changed.

Select.description: One choice from a list that stays collapsed until opened: a Button trigger that shows the chosen option and opens a popup list, where a check mark shows the chosen option, with a label above it, a description, an error and native form participation.

props.name: ref
props.description: The trigger, the button that shows the chosen option and opens the list.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-select.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: items
props.description: The options of the list, in order, each with a value, a label and whether it is disabled.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value in a controlled select, or null for none, which shows the placeholder; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The chosen option's value an uncontrolled select starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without it, nothing is chosen and the trigger shows the placeholder.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the chosen option's value with a form under this name, through a hidden input.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits: the browser refuses the form and moves focus to the trigger while nothing is chosen.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: What the trigger shows while nothing is chosen, such as Choose an owner.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: A hint for the browser's autofill, such as country, set on the hidden input.

props.name: variant
props.description: The trigger's Button variant, to suit its surroundings: secondary, a filled pill, for the page; or outline, a bordered pill, for panes, dialogs, rows and toolbars, where a fill would blend with the surface.

props.name: size
props.description: The trigger's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the trigger takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. The popup's rows take the row height of the scale.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Sheet.description: A panel that slides in over the page from an edge of the window, for filters, details, an inspector or choices: a side sheet from the end or the start edge, or a bottom sheet. It is a modal by default, which traps focus and returns it on close, or beside the page with modal false. A side sheet takes the whole width of a compact window, and a swipe toward its edge closes it. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the sheet's surface.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the sheet is open, for a sheet the application controls with onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether a sheet the application doesn't control is open on the first render.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the requested state, and why, when the sheet asks to open or close: from the trigger, Escape, an outside press, the close button, a swipe toward its edge or a DialogClose. Not called for a dismissal that pending blocks.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the sheet, such as a Button. It reports the sheet it opens, and focus returns to it on close. Omit it for a sheet the application opens with open.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge of the window the sheet slides in from: end, the right in left-to-right text, or start, the left, as a side sheet as tall as the window; or bottom, as a bottom sheet as wide as the window up to 40 rem and as tall as its content. start and end follow the text direction, so they are mirrored in right-to-left text.

props.name: title
props.description: The sheet's heading and accessible name, such as Filters. Without one, name the sheet with aria-label.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The sheet's accessible name where it has no visible title.

props.name: description
props.description: Muted text under the title that describes the sheet to assistive technology too.

props.name: children
props.description: The content under the heading, such as filters, details or choices. It scrolls.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions at the end of the content, such as Apply, with the primary action last.

props.name: closeButton
props.description: Whether the sheet shows its close button, a CloseButton at the end of the heading. Leave it out only where the sheet holds another control that closes it.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name.

props.name: width
props.description: A side sheet's width: md, 24 rem, for details and filters; lg, 44 rem, for content-heavy panels such as tables and comparisons; or any CSS length, such as min(20rem, 100% - 2rem). md takes the whole width of a compact window, lg of a compact or medium one, where the page beside it would be a sliver. A bottom sheet ignores it.

props.name: modal
props.description: true traps focus in the sheet over a backdrop, hides the page from assistive technology, blocks presses on it and locks its scroll. false leaves the page usable beside the sheet, for an inspector; it then closes when focus or a press goes outside it, unless disablePointerDismissal.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Keep the sheet open on presses outside it, and a non-modal sheet also when focus moves outside, such as an inspector beside the page it inspects. Escape and the close buttons still close it.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the sheet opens, as a ref or a function of how it was opened. By default focus moves to the first element inside that takes Tab, such as the close button, or to the sheet itself when opened by touch or when nothing inside takes focus.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the sheet closes, as a ref or a function of how it closed, such as the main content after a navigation. By default focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus when it opened.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started from the sheet is in progress: Escape, outside presses, swipes and the close button cannot dismiss it until pending returns to false, and the sheet reports busy.

Skeleton.description: A placeholder in the shape of content that is loading, such as a line of text or a row: a block with rounded corners on the neutral fill, which pulses unless people prefer reduced motion. It is hidden from assistive technology; put placeholders in a LoadingState, which names the region.

props.name: width
props.description: The placeholder's width, as a CSS length, such as 38% or 12rem, for the content it stands for. Without it, the placeholder fills the width of its container.

props.name: height
props.description: The placeholder's height, as a CSS length, such as 1.25rem for a heading or 3.5rem for a row.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strong the fill is: muted, the neutral fill, or default, one step stronger, for a placeholder that stands out among the others, such as a title.

Slider.description: A value in a range, chosen by dragging a thumb along a track, pressing the track or with the keyboard, with its label and current value above the track and an optional description below.

props.name: label
props.description: The value's name above the track, such as Opacity. It names the slider, and pressing it moves focus to the slider.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the track, such as what the value applies to, linked to the slider as its description.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of a controlled slider; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled slider starts with; a native form reset returns to it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value while it changes, by dragging, pressing the track or with the keyboard, as often as the thumb moves.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Receives the value once a change is complete: when the thumb is released or the track pressed, and after each key. Use it for work that runs once per change, such as saving.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value, at the start of the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value, at the end of the track.

props.name: step
props.description: The distance between the values the slider can take, counted from min; an arrow key moves by it.

props.name: largeStep
props.default: a tenth of the range in whole steps, at least one step
props.description: The change of Page Up, Page Down and an arrow key with Shift.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: The value as people read it above the track and assistive technology announces it, such as (value) => `${value}%`. Without it, the number shows in the locale.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown number: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the slider; it can't be focused or moved, and forms leave it out.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the value with a form under this name.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of a form the slider belongs to when it sits outside of it.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: The native range input, for example to focus it.

Spinner.description: Work of unknown length in a small area, such as a panel that is updating: an arc in the control blue that turns, and keeps turning slowly with a reduced-motion preference. With a label it is a progress bar named by it; without one it is hidden from assistive technology. The hook --env-spinner-color recolors it, such as to a button's label color.

props.name: label
props.description: The work it stands for, such as Refreshing members, which names the spinner as a progress bar for assistive technology. Leave it out where a busy control or region already says so; the spinner is then hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.description: sm, 1 rem, inside controls and beside a line of text; md, 1.5 rem, beside a heading or in a panel; or lg, 3 rem, in the middle of a region whose content is on its way.

Stat.Group.description: Stats on one surface, a pane's fill by default, in as many even columns as fit; they wrap as space runs out. Use the muted background for a group on a pane. A group named with aria-label or aria-labelledby is exposed as a group, so assistive technology announces the name.

props.name: background
props.description: The group's fill, as for Surface: default on the page, or muted for a group on a pane, so its stats stand apart; page or raised where those fit.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, such as 4 for 1 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width, as for Surface.

Stat.Root.description: A labelled key figure for a dashboard, such as Active projects 128, with an optional trend and description. It has no surface of its own; Stat.Group puts several on one, or a Card holds one.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure measures, such as Active projects, in muted text above it.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, formatted by the application with its unit, such as 1,284 or 2.5 days, or an AnimatedNumber that rolls to new values. It shows large, in tabular digits.

props.name: description
props.description: A muted note below the figure, after the trend, such as the period: Last 30 days.

props.name: trend
props.description: The change since an earlier period, such as up and +12% from last month, shown below the figure as a direction icon and text in its tone.

Surface.description: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own: spacing between its children, alignment and behaviour come from what it holds, such as a Column. Card and other containers build on it.

props.name: background
props.description: The fill: default, the background of panes and side regions; muted, the background of rows; page, the page background; or raised, a block that stands out on a pane.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, from 1 (0.25 rem) to 9 (4 rem), such as 5 for 1.5 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width.

props.name: radius
props.description: The corner radius: xl, the large 1.75 rem corners of panes; sm, 0.5 rem for small blocks; full, fully rounded ends for a toolbar or a bar of filters; or none, square, for a region that meets the edges of its container.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render the surface as, for its meaning, such as render={<section />}, or another component to render it onto without a wrapper, such as a Column that lays out its content: the surface's class, style and attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks, and `SurfaceProps['ref']` is a ref to the default element, so a wrapper can forward it to one.

Switch.description: An on/off setting that takes effect at once: a native checkbox with the switch role, drawn as a track and a thumb, with its label beside it.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native checkbox with the switch role, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props, such as name, reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The switch's class, on its root element, the label around the track and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: label
props.description: The setting the switch turns on or off, such as Show completed tasks, beside the track. It names the switch, stays the same in both states, and pressing it toggles the switch too. Without it, name the switch with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether a controlled switch is on; update it from onCheckedChange.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled switch starts on; a native form reset returns it to this state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Receives the new state each time people turn the switch on or off.

Table.Body.description: The data rows of a table, a native tbody, separated by hairlines.

Table.Cell.description: A data cell, a native td, with a label that names its value while rows stack.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name, shown before the value while a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows. Assistive technology reads the column header instead.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Head.description: The header rows of a table, a native thead, which hold the column headers.

Table.HeaderCell.description: A header cell, a native th that heads its column, or its row with scope="row". With onSortChange it sorts its column; in a table with resizable columns it holds the column's resize handle.

props.name: sortDirection
props.description: The column's sort order: aria-sort on the header and the arrow in its sort button. Use it with onSortChange; without it only sets aria-sort.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: The header becomes a button across the cell that asks the application to sort the rows by this column, with the order pressing it asks for: descending while the column is sorted ascending, ascending otherwise. The application sorts the rows and sets sortDirection.

props.name: sortLabel
props.default: '{header} sort {next order}', from EnvUIProvider's messages.table.sortAscending and sortDescending
props.description: Accessible name of the sort button, which says what pressing it does: the header's name followed by "sort ascending", or by "sort descending" while the column is sorted ascending.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the column's resize handle, "Resize" followed by the header's name.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Root.description: A semantic data table on a rounded surface, in a focusable region that scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table and its scroll region when there is no caption. A table needs a caption, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby, which names its region too.

props.name: caption
props.description: A visible caption above the rows that names the table and its scroll region, in place of aria-label or aria-labelledby. Under a sticky header it scrolls away with the rows.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only the cells' block padding, never the text. Buttons, icon buttons and fields in the cells take the small control height in every density, unless they set a size.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: The header row stays at the top of the region while the rows scroll beneath it. The region then scrolls vertically too, so give it a height through regionClassName or the surrounding layout.

props.name: regionClassName
props.description: Class of the scroll region around the table, for example to limit its height.

props.name: narrowLayout
props.description: What the table does when its region is narrower than stackBelow: scroll keeps the columns and scrolls sideways; stack shows each body row as a block that starts with its first cell, followed by the other cells with their labels. The header row is then visually hidden. A container query on the region decides it, so the server's markup and the first paint already stack; a stacking region fills the width its context gives it.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: The region width below which a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows: a CSS length such as 60rem or 480px, or a number of pixels, such as 600 or "600". Wide tables, such as seven sortable columns, need more.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the rows stack and with false when the columns return, as the table reads its layout once it is in the document, for example to show another sort control while the header row is hidden; a table that leaves while its rows stack reports false. The region has data-stacked from then on while the rows stack; style stacked rows with a container query on env-table, which applies before hydration, rather than through it.

props.name: columnWidths
props.description: Column widths in percent of the table width, in column order and adding up to 100, for widths the application controls with onColumnWidthsChange. Set widths fix the columns: long words wrap and nowrap cells end with an ellipsis.

props.name: defaultColumnWidths
props.description: Starting column widths, in percent, when the table owns them; other defaults start them over. Double-clicking a resize handle restores them, or else the widths a controlled table started with.

props.name: onColumnWidthsChange
props.description: Called with every column's width when people resize a column.

props.name: minColumnWidths
props.description: Smallest width of each column in percent, in column order, or one value for every column.

props.name: resizableColumns
props.description: People can resize the columns with a handle at the end of each header cell but the last, which moves the boundary to the next column and keeps the table's width. Needs columnWidths or defaultColumnWidths.

Table.Row.description: A row of a table, a native tr, which can highlight on hover or be selected.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row highlights on hover and while focus is inside it, for rows that open something through a link or button in a cell. It adds no behavior of its own.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row is selected: it reports aria-selected and takes the selection colors, with a bar at its start. Pass false to the other rows of a table whose rows can be selected; unset, a row reports no selection state.

Tabs.description: Switches between panels of related content in one place: a rail of the buttons you supply, each a tab linked to its panel, with selection from the keyboard and panels that fade as they change. The selected tab keeps its button's own look; the others are quiet on the rail.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs in order, each with its value, button and panel content.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tab list's accessible name, such as Project views.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected tab's value, for controlled tabs; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab that uncontrolled tabs start on.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the tab people select, by pressing it or from the keyboard.

props.name: activation
props.description: automatic selects a tab as the arrow keys move focus to it; manual only moves focus, and Enter or Space selects, for panels that take a moment to show.

props.name: orientation
props.description: horizontal puts the tabs in a row, moved through with the left and right arrow keys; vertical in a column, with the up and down arrow keys. The panels stay below the list either way.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Keep the panels of unselected tabs mounted and hidden, so their state, such as a draft or a scroll position, survives switching; otherwise a panel unmounts once it has faded out.

props.name: renderList
props.description: Places the tab list in a layout of your own, such as beside a heading: it receives the list and returns what to render in its place, with the list in it once. The panels stay below.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: A class for the tab list, the rail that holds the tabs.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: A class for every panel.

props.name: fill
props.description: The selected panel takes the height left below the list, for content that fills a region, such as a canvas; give the tabs a height, for example as a flex child.

props.name: size
props.description: The rail's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. The tabs inside are a little shorter. lg gives tabs as tall as md buttons; sm suits a toolbar or a bar, beside a SegmentedControl or buttons of size sm.

Text.description: Semantic native text with typography and color from the shared token scale.

props.name: variant
props.description: The text style: display for a page's introduction, body for running text, headline for a page's heading, title for a section's, body-sm for supporting text and caption for the smallest notes. body-sm and caption are muted unless emphasis says otherwise.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strong the text is: default, the text color; muted, for supporting text; subtle, the weakest, for text that should recede, such as a hint beside a value.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<h2 />} for a heading or render={<span />} inside a line; a p by default. The text's class and attributes merge into its props.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a p by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks, and `TextProps['ref']` is a ref to the default element, so a wrapper can forward it to one.

TextField.description: A labelled single-line text input: a native input with a floating label, a description and an error, at the control height in an outline or ghost look, or taller as the floating and underline variants, with an optional start icon, end action, prefix and suffix.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
