props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, with a thin border, at the control height; floating, an outlined field 3.5 rem tall whose label rests inside and floats into the outline, for long forms on a page; underline, as tall, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or ghost, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon at the start of the field, such as Search or Mail.

props.name: endAction
props.description: A control at the end of the field, such as an IconButton that reveals or copies the value; name it with aria-label. A button that sets no variant takes ghost here.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, where it rests while the field is empty and floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it, such as a search in a toolbar: the label still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another, as a table cell does. A button beside a field takes the field's size. Floating and underline fields have their own height.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

Textarea.description: A labelled text area for text over several lines: a native textarea in the text field's frame, at a fixed height that scrolls and resizes from its bottom edge, or growing with its content.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native text area, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, underline or ghost. A text area is always tall, with its label resting at the top, so it has no floating variant.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the text as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: sizing
props.description: How the height follows the text: fixed keeps its height, scrolls and resizes from the bottom edge, by dragging it or with the arrow keys; content grows and shrinks with the text.

props.name: rows
props.description: The lines the field shows: with fixed sizing, its height in rows, at least 7.5 rem; with content sizing, the lines it starts at and shrinks back to, also under 7.5 rem. Without rows, both start at 7.5 rem.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Theme.description: An explicit, scoped theme: a color scheme, a contrast and a scale, which nested Themes and envUI's popups keep. Theme preference and persistence belong to the app.

props.name: theme
props.description: The color scheme.

props.name: contrast
props.description: `high` for the high-contrast colors; `standard` keeps the standard ones even while the system asks for more contrast; `system` follows `prefers-contrast: more`. Defaults to the contrast of the enclosing Theme, and to `system` outside any. It wins over a `data-env-contrast` attribute passed to the Theme; left out, such an attribute of `high` or `standard` sets the contrast, for the boundary, its nested Themes and its popups alike.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale of everything inside: comfortable, or compact for a desktop productivity app. Use one scale per app or window, and another only on a Theme around a whole region, such as a docked inspector. Defaults to the scale of the enclosing Theme, and to comfortable outside any. It wins over a `data-env-scale` attribute passed to the Theme.

ThemePreferenceProvider.description: Owns the theme preference: persistence, the system theme and document-root theming.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key; match the bootstrap script's. Defaults to "env-theme".

props.name: defaultPreference
props.description: Used when nothing is stored. Defaults to "system".

props.name: applyToDocument
props.description: Theme the document root as well as this subtree (default). Root theming covers the page background, native controls, portals rendered by other libraries and the content of every theme-color meta tag, which takes the canvas color. One provider per document applies to it: pass false to any other, nested in it or beside it. In development, envUI reports two providers that both apply.

props.name: contrast
props.description: Contrast of the Theme boundary around the children, and of the document root with applyToDocument: high, standard, or system to follow `prefers-contrast: more`, as on Theme. Defaults to the contrast of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a contrast the page set on the root, and otherwise system. With system, the provider removes from the root only a contrast that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged: a provider, this one or one before it, or the bootstrap script. Pass a contrast that is fixed for the application to createThemeBootstrapScript too, so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale, comfortable or compact for a desktop productivity app, as on Theme: of the Theme boundary around the children, and, marked as envUI's own, of the document root with applyToDocument. Without it, the boundary takes the scale of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a scale the page set on the root, so the application, the page and its portals share it, and otherwise comfortable. The root keeps a scale the page set but drops one that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged. Pass the same scale to createThemeBootstrapScript so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the Theme boundary around the children.

ThemeRadioGroup.description: The theme choice for a Menu: System, Light and Dark as radio items. Inside a ThemePreferenceProvider it shows and stores the provider's preference; value and onValueChange connect it to a theme the application stores itself.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen preference: system, light or dark.

props.name: onValueChange
props.default: the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider's setPreference, which stores the choice
props.description: Called with the preference chosen, for an application that stores the theme itself.

props.name: label
props.description: A small heading above the choices, which names the group. Leave it out inside a submenu, which its row already names.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of a heading elsewhere in the menu that names the group, in place of label.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after a choice. Off by default, so people see the theme change with the menu still open.

ThemeToggle.description: Switches between the light and dark themes and stores the choice.

props.name: size
props.description: As Button's: the height, and the width, of the square button.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis, as Button's. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else secondary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning, as Button's: accent on a primary button only, and danger on a primary, outline, ghost or text one. A secondary button is always neutral.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name; without it, Switch to dark theme or Switch to light theme, or EnvUIProvider's messages.themeToggle.

TimePicker.description: A field for a time of day that shows the value in the reader's locale and opens wheels of its hours, minutes every `minuteStep` and, on a 12-hour clock, the day's halves to choose it.

props.name: value
props.description: The value: a time of day as HH:mm on the 24-hour clock. null, or an empty string, for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores; none by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the new value as HH:mm, or null once the field is cleared.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest time, as HH:mm; earlier times are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest time, as HH:mm; later times are unavailable.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: The minutes between the times the list offers, from 1 to 60. A value between them still shows in the list, in its place.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown value and the list's times, with its own 12- or 24-hour clock: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the field shows the value: Intl.DateTimeFormat options, by default the short time style.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the field's clear button and text of the popup's.

props.name: nowLabel
props.description: The popup's shortcut to the current time.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's button, which shows the value and opens the popup.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the value is submitted under with a form.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is needed: an empty field keeps its form from submitting and takes focus.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The value can be read and focused but not changed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while the field is empty and its label floats or is hidden.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, at the control height, or floating, 3.5 rem tall with room for its label, for long forms on a page.

props.name: size
props.description: The field's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label inside the field, where it floats into the outline while the field has a value, focus or its popup open. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A clear button in the field and in the popup removes the value.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open; with `onOpenChange` it controls it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popup starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Toast.Provider.description: Hosts the notifications that useToast shows: brief feedback at the edge of the window, announced and dismissed after a few seconds or by people. Put one near the root of the application; it renders a region for each placement in a portal, in the theme of the place it is rendered.

props.name: children
props.description: The application, or the part of it whose components call useToast.

props.name: defaultPlacement
props.description: Where notifications show unless show names a placement: bottom-end, stacking upward from the bottom corner at the end of the line, or top-center, stacking downward from the top.

props.name: visibleLimit
props.description: How many notifications each placement shows at once, a positive integer. The newest stay visible; older ones wait behind a count of hidden notifications and come back as newer ones close. Danger notifications always show, and take their places first.

Toolbar.Button.description: An icon-only button of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows; disabled, it leaves the arrow keys' path.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as FormatBold.

props.name: label
props.description: The action's name, such as Bold: assistive technology announces it, and the tooltip shows it on hover and focus.

props.name: pressed
props.description: For a button that turns something on and off, such as Bold: whether it is on. It is announced as pressed and drawn selected. Leave it out for a button that acts once, such as Undo.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keyboard shortcut that does the same, such as Ctrl+B, with keys joined by +: the tooltip shows it, and aria-keyshortcuts announces it, in ARIA's key names, such as Control+B. A sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+B, shows its keys without the attribute, as in Menu.

props.name: variant
props.description: As Button's; ghost by default, from the toolbar.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

Toolbar.Group.description: Controls of a toolbar that belong together, such as the text styles.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the group, such as Text style, where its controls belong together.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in the group.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the group as, such as a ButtonGroup.

Toolbar.Link.description: An icon-only link of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as Help.

props.name: label
props.description: The destination's name, which assistive technology announces and the tooltip shows.

Toolbar.Root.description: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, such as a text editor's formatting: one tab stop, with the arrow keys moving between its controls (the APG toolbar pattern). Buttons the application puts inside take the ghost variant unless they set another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the toolbar for assistive technology, such as Formatting.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the controls run in, and which arrow keys move between them.

props.name: size
props.description: The height of the buttons inside, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the control height of the container.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control inside.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether the arrow keys move from the last control to the first and back.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the toolbar as, such as a ButtonGroup that connects its buttons; the toolbar's class, attributes and keyboard handling merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls: Toolbar.Button, Toolbar.Link, Toolbar.Group and Toolbar.Separator.

Toolbar.Separator.description: A line between groups of a toolbar's controls, across the toolbar's direction.

Tooltip.description: A short label beside a control, shown while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus, such as an icon-only button's name or why a control is disabled. It closes on Esc and when the control is pressed, and stays closed while the control's own popup, such as a menu, is open. Native props and ref go to the control, so a Tooltip can be the trigger of a Menu.Root or Popover; popupClassName styles the tooltip's popup.

props.name: content
props.description: What the tooltip shows: a short, supplementary text, such as an icon-only control's name or why a control is disabled. While it is open, a control with a name of its own is described by it (aria-describedby); never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: children
props.description: The one control it describes, such as an IconButton, which takes the trigger's props and ref, and the Tooltip's own native props and ref. Around a Menu.Root, Popover, Dialog, Sheet or ConfirmDialog, the tooltip describes their `trigger`; around a HoverCard, it shows nothing. A disabled control is wrapped in an element that hovering opens the tooltip on. Around a button, link, tab or menu item, it is focusable and carries the control's name, role and state, reported disabled, so keyboard focus opens it too. One element: text, a Fragment or a component that doesn't pass the ref on to its element gets no tooltip, and says so while developing.

props.name: ref
props.description: The control's ref, as the Tooltip passes its props on to the control, such as when the Tooltip is the `trigger` of a Menu.Root or Popover, which give their trigger a ref.

props.name: popupClassName
props.description: Class of the tooltip's popup, beside env-tooltip.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the control it opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. Where the window has no room, it flips to the other side.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the control before the tooltip opens; keyboard focus opens it at once.

TopBar.description: The bar at the top of an application or a screen: start content, such as a navigation button or the application's mark, the title, which truncates first, and the actions at the end, in one row that never wraps, at the top bar height. It can stick to the top as the page scrolls, show page progress along its bottom edge, or be the window's own title bar.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the title, at the inline start: a navigation IconButton, such as one that opens a navigation drawer, a back IconButton, or the application's mark.

props.name: title
props.description: The title, such as the application's or the section's name. It truncates before the start content and the actions shrink. It is no heading: the page's own heading is its PageHeader's.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions at the inline end, such as a search trigger, a theme toggle and an account menu, in the order people read them.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keeps the bar at the top of the scrolling area as it scrolls, for a bar in a page whose document scrolls. In a Scaffold's top bar region it is unneeded: the body scrolls under it.

props.name: titleBar
props.description: The bar is the window's title bar, in an installed web app or a desktop shell that draws its own (the Window Controls Overlay): empty space drags the window, it leaves room for the window controls the system draws, the title is centered, and its controls are small, with buttons that set no variant ghost. Put it in a Scaffold with topBarSpan="full".

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows page progress along the bar's bottom edge, such as while the next page loads.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The progress bar's name.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, such as render={<header />} for a bar outside a Scaffold, which then is the page's banner; a div by default, as Scaffold's top bar region is the banner.

Tree.description: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies such as file trees. The application passes the visible rows and owns expansion and selection; the tree owns focus, keyboard navigation and scrolling. It fills its parent's height, scrolls itself and renders only the rows in view.

props.name: items
props.description: The visible rows in order, flattened: an expanded row is followed by its visible descendants. The application owns expansion; collapsing a row removes its descendants from items.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tree's accessible name, such as Files.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected row's id: it takes the navigation selection colors and scrolls into view when it changes. The application sets it, usually from onAction.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called when people open a row: with preview true on a single click and Space, and false on a double click and Enter. Expandable rows call it too, and disabled rows don't.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the row and its new state from a press on its chevron, the right arrow key on a collapsed row and the left arrow key on an expanded one, mirrored in right-to-left text. The application updates items.

props.name: contextMenu
props.description: Menu items for the row people right-click, or press Shift+F10 or the Menu key on, or for the tree's empty area when the item is null. Without it, the browser's own context menu stays.

props.name: contextMenuLabel
props.description: The context menu's accessible name.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only their block padding, never the text or the icons. In the comfortable scale sm rows are 1.75 rem tall and md rows 2.25 rem. Under a coarse pointer every row is at least 2.75 rem.

props.name: className
props.description: A class for the tree, the element that scrolls.

props.name: style
props.description: The tree's inline style, such as a height.

props.name: ref
props.description: The tree element, which scrolls and holds focus.

avatarHue.description: The hue a name gives an avatar: the same name always gives the same hue, on every page and in every session, and different names spread across the hues. Letter case and surrounding spaces do not count.

countDiffLines.description: How many lines a change adds and removes, as a DiffStat shows them.
countDiffLines.signature: (before: string, after: string, filename?: string): { additions: number; deletions: number; }

createRichTextExtensions.description: The Tiptap extensions RichTextEditor and RichText share: formatting, lists and task lists, tables, safe links and images, Markdown with raw HTML kept as text, a placeholder and references. options.extensions are added after them, for other Tiptap integrations that need the same schema.

createThemeBootstrapScript.description: Inline script for the document head. It themes the root element before the first paint, so a saved or system dark theme does not flash light while the application loads, and a high or standard contrast applies from the start.
createThemeBootstrapScript.signature: ({ storageKey, defaultPreference, contrast, scale, }?: ThemeBootstrapOptions): string

formatRelativeTime.description: A moment as text relative to another, by default the current time, such as "in 2 days", "3 hours ago" or "just now", through Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. An invalid moment gives an empty string; an invalid now is ignored, as by RelativeTime, for the current time.

installDevMode.description: Installs dev mode: `window.envui.layout` with `describe()`, `check()` and `at()`, a toggle button in the corner and Alt+Shift+D, which open the 3D view and the inspector over the page. Load it in development only, so production builds contain none of it: if (import.meta.env.DEV) { void import('@envsemble/envui/dev').then(({ installDevMode }) => installDevMode()); } Calling it again returns the dev mode already installed, until it is uninstalled.

readPanesSize.description: The width Panes keeps under its `persist` key, read from a Cookie header, such as the request's on the server, or from `document.cookie`. Render Panes.Root with it as `persistedSize`, on the server and in the browser alike, so the server's markup has the width people chose and nothing moves as the page hydrates: <Panes.Root persist="inbox" persistedSize={readPanesSize(cookieHeader, 'inbox')}> Returns undefined where no width is kept under the key.
readPanesSize.signature: (cookies: string | null | undefined, key: string): number | undefined

resolveNavigationForms.description: The form that shows at each window class: the one asked for, else the nearest one given, else none. Worked out from the props alone, so the server's markup has it, and CSS shows it at its width.
resolveNavigationForms.signature: (navigation: ScaffoldNavigation | undefined, forms: ScaffoldForms | undefined): Record<WindowClass, NavigationForm | "none">

useContainerSize.description: The size of an element, kept up to date as it changes: its inline and block size in CSS pixels, along its writing mode, from a ResizeObserver. It is undefined on the server and until the element is measured, which happens before the browser paints it; an element that stops being rendered, such as one in a hidden tab panel, keeps its last size until it shows again. Pass a ref object, read once the element mounts, or the element itself, such as one kept in state by a callback ref. Prefer a container query (`@container`) where only styles change. const panel = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); const size = useContainerSize(panel); const narrow = size !== undefined && size.inlineSize < 640;
useContainerSize.signature: <T extends Element>(target: RefObject<T | null> | T | null, options?: ContainerSizeOptions): ContainerSize | undefined

useLocale.description: The locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider, for formatting in step with envUI, or undefined where no provider sets one: the runtime's locale applies then.

useTheme.description: The theme of the nearest Theme, including across React portals: its color scheme, contrast and scale. A portal of the application's own takes it with `<Theme {...useTheme()}>`. A contrast of `system` leaves the choice to the stylesheet, which reads `prefers-contrast: more`.

useThemePreference.description: The theme preference from the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider.

useToast.description: Shows and dismisses notifications through the nearest Toast.Provider: show, dismiss and clear. Throws outside a provider.

tokens.usage: Use a token through its CSS custom property, such as var(--env-color-fg-muted), in CSS that styles the application. These system tokens and the components' part names are the public contract: CSS may target a component's part classes and state attributes (each component's parts), which are versioned, so a rename or removal is a breaking change. Component tokens, the custom properties a component declares for itself such as --env-card-padding, are private and may change in any release; set the system tokens instead.

items.description: The blue fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name, and the fill of an avatar with hue="blue".
The amber fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The green fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The purple fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The red fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The slate fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The teal fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The violet fill, one of the hues an avatar takes from its name.
The initials of an avatar, at least 4.5:1 on every fill, and 7:1 at high contrast.
The default figure of an avatar without an image, on any of its fills.
A solid accent fill, such as a solid accent badge; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent accent tint of badges and info alerts.
Controls in the accent tone without a fill at rest, such as an alert’s dismiss button: transparent, as color.bg.neutral.subtle is.
The state layer of a control without a fill in the accent tone, such as an info alert’s dismiss button, under the pointer: the accent text color at 14%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The accent state layer while pressed: the accent text color at 22%.

The brand fill of primary actions, chosen radios and the chosen calendar day; paired with fg.on-emphasis. In dark and at high contrast, checked checkboxes, switches that are on, sliders, meters and spinners take it too: a soft blue with dark marks at 4.5:1.
A primary action under the pointer.
A primary action while pressed.
The translucent halo of a slider thumb that is dragged: the blue of the thumb at 16%, in every theme and at high contrast.

The saturated brand fill of checked checkboxes, switches that are on, sliders, meters and spinners in the light theme at standard contrast, with white marks, the check and the thumb, at 3:1. The dark theme and high contrast put those controls on the emphasis fill instead; in dark this fill, which keeps 3:1 against the surfaces, would put white text below 4.5:1.
A checked control under the pointer.
A checked control while pressed.
A solid danger fill; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent danger tint of badges and alerts.
The danger fill of destructive actions and error toasts in both themes; paired with fg.on-strong.
A destructive action under the pointer: lighter, as in 0.7, at the lightest grade that keeps white labels at 4.5:1.
A destructive action while pressed. It can’t lighten further without its white label falling below 4.5:1, so it settles halfway back.
Controls in the danger tone without a fill at rest, such as an alert’s dismiss button: transparent, as color.bg.neutral.subtle is.
The state layer of a control without a fill in the danger tone, such as an error alert’s dismiss button, under the pointer: the danger text color at 14%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The danger state layer while pressed: the danger text color at 22%.
The default surface: Surface, navigation, standard menus.
An interactive default surface, such as a card or a list row, under the pointer.
An interactive default surface while pressed. Muted text and an inset focus ring keep their minimums on it.
A solid done fill; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent done tint of badges.
Text fields and other inputs.
The accent purple of important actions in both themes; paired with fg.on-strong.
An important action under the pointer.
An important action while pressed.
The information fill of toasts in both themes; paired with fg.on-strong.
A control on the information toast under the pointer. Its white label keeps 4.5:1.
A control on the information toast while pressed. Its white label keeps 4.5:1.
The page color at half strength, which leans a pill on a button’s fill back toward the page instead of adding another fill, as a diff stat in a tab does.
The muted surface: Surface background="muted", radio rows. Grayer than the default surface in the light theme, so cards stand apart from a pane, and lighter than it in the dark theme.
An interactive muted surface under the pointer.
An interactive muted surface while pressed.

A navigation item that isn’t selected, under the pointer: a blue-gray tint in light, deeper than the selection so it doesn’t read as selected; in dark and at high contrast, a gray, since a blue tint there would read as the selection.
A navigation item that isn’t selected, while pressed. Its label and an inset focus ring keep their minimums on it, which puts it one grade deeper than the hover in light.
A solid neutral fill, such as a solid neutral badge; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent neutral fill of secondary buttons, tab rails, chips, switch tracks, meter tracks and skeletons: a layer of the text color, so it keeps its tone on every surface.
The neutral fill under the pointer.
The neutral fill while pressed.
The dark neutral fill of tooltips and neutral toasts in both themes; paired with fg.on-strong.
A control on the strong neutral fill under the pointer.
A control on the strong neutral fill while pressed.
Controls without a fill at rest, such as quiet buttons, inactive tabs and menubar triggers.
The state layer over a control without a fill, under the pointer.
The state layer over a control without a fill, while pressed.
The scrim behind dialogs and the command palette: the dark page color at 55%.
The lighter scrim behind a sheet that leaves the page usable, such as a supporting pane over its main pane: the dark page color at 30%.
The page behind all content: the app frame, title bars and Surface background="page".
An interactive page-colored surface under the pointer.
An interactive page-colored surface while pressed.
Popups over the page: menus, Select lists, popovers, the composer. They take elevation 2.
A highlighted row in a popup.
A pressed row in a popup.
A raised surface: Surface background="raised", dialogs, rows on a contrasting surface, outlined buttons.
An interactive raised surface under the pointer.
An interactive raised surface while pressed.

Selected navigation items, tree and table rows, Select options and drop targets; paired with fg.on-selected. A blue tint in light and a blue-gray in dark, distinct from the other items around it, at rest and under the pointer: ΔEOK 0.03 or more, 0.04 at high contrast.
A selected item under the pointer: visibly deeper than the selection, and distinct from an unselected item under the pointer.
A selected item while pressed. Muted text and an inset focus ring keep their minimums on it.
A solid success fill; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent success tint of badges and alerts.
The teal success fill of toasts in both themes; paired with fg.on-strong.
A control on the success toast, its dismiss button, under the pointer. Its white label keeps 4.5:1.
A control on the success toast while pressed. Its white label keeps 4.5:1.
Controls in the success tone without a fill at rest, such as an alert’s dismiss button: transparent, as color.bg.neutral.subtle is.
The state layer of a control without a fill in the success tone, such as a success alert’s dismiss button, under the pointer: the success text color at 14%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The success state layer while pressed: the success text color at 22%.
A solid warning fill; paired with fg.on-emphasis.
The translucent warning tint of badges and alerts.
Controls in the warning tone without a fill at rest, such as an alert’s dismiss button: transparent, as color.bg.neutral.subtle is.
The state layer of a control without a fill in the warning tone, such as a warning alert’s dismiss button, under the pointer: the warning text color at 14%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The warning state layer while pressed: the warning text color at 22%.
A decorative edge in the accent tone, around an outlined badge: the accent text color at 55%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The active border and label of a focused field, and today’s ring in a calendar.
An active field border under the pointer.
An active field border while pressed.
The faint edge of an info alert: the accent text color at 28%, in every theme and at high contrast.
A decorative edge in the danger tone, around an outlined badge and a message that failed to send: the danger text color at 55%, in every theme and at high contrast.
The border of an invalid field.
An invalid field border under the pointer.
An invalid field border while pressed.
The faint edge of an error alert: the danger text color at 28%, in every theme and at high contrast.

The edge of the strong danger fill where it floats, on error toasts. In light the fill is dark on a light page, so its edge is the fill a step darker, about 1.3:1 from it: it reads as the fill’s own edge rather than a light halo, and still sets the fill apart from a surface of its color. High contrast keeps that step, from the darker high-contrast fill, far above 4.5:1 on the page. In dark, where the fill is lighter than the page as every popup is, it is the popup edge of elevation 2: color.border.muted, and color.border.default at high contrast. A dark edge, unlike the 0.7 alias color.border-strong, which is the light divider color, border.muted.
The boundary of a control that has no other edge: outlined fields and buttons, the track of a switch that is off. At least 3:1 on every surface.
A control boundary under the pointer.
A control boundary while pressed.
A decorative edge in the done tone, around an outlined badge: the done text color at 55%, in every theme and at high contrast.
Focus rings: at least 3:1 against what they are drawn on.

The edge of the strong information fill where it floats, on information toasts. In light the fill is dark on a light page, so its edge is the fill a step darker, about 1.3:1 from it: it reads as the fill’s own edge rather than a light halo, and still sets the fill apart from a surface of its color. High contrast keeps that step, from the darker high-contrast fill, far above 4.5:1 on the page. In dark, where the fill is lighter than the page as every popup is, it is the popup edge of elevation 2: color.border.muted, and color.border.default at high contrast. A dark edge, unlike the 0.7 alias color.border-strong, which is the light divider color, border.muted.
A neutral inner edge that defines content of any color, such as the color picker’s area: black at 5% in both themes.

Decorative dividers and outlines that are not a control’s only boundary: table lines, title bars, Markdown rules, keyboard keys, and the hairline edge of every elevated popup, which the elevation shadow and the content already identify.
A decorative outline under the pointer, such as a resize handle or a pager link.
